cz.2006.1.1.reviewed_statement: A sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive integers has the property that for every $n\ge 1$ we have $a_{n+1}=a_n+b_n$, where $b_n$ is the number whose digits are those of $a_n$ in reverse order (unlike the notation of $a_n$, the notation of $b_n$ may begin with one or more zeros). For example, for $a_1=170$ we get $a_2=241$, $a_3=383$, $a_4=766$, $\dots$ Decide whether $a_7$ can be a prime.
cz.2006.1.1.rationale: Digit-reversal recurrence and primality of a term.

cz.2006.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers such that the equation $$(x+m)(x+n)=x+m+n$$ has at least one integer solution. Prove that $$\frac{1}{2}<\frac{m}{n}<2.$$
cz.2006.1.2.rationale: Integer quadratic root forcing bounds on two parameters.

cz.2006.1.3.reviewed_statement:
In a triangle $ABC$ which is not equilateral, let $K$ be the intersection of the bisector of the interior angle $BAC$ with the side $BC$, and $L$ the intersection of the bisector of the interior angle $ABC$ with the side $AC$. Further, let $S$ be the incentre, $O$ the circumcentre and $V$ the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$. Prove that the following two statements are equivalent:

a) The line $KL$ is tangent to the circumcircles of the triangles $ALS$, $BVS$ and $BKS$.

b) The points $A$, $B$, $K$, $L$ and $O$ lie on one circle.

cz.2006.2.4.reviewed_statement: A segment $AB$ is given in the plane. Determine the locus of the centroids of all acute triangles $ABC$ with the following property: the vertices $A$ and $B$, the orthocentre $V$ and the incentre $S$ of the triangle $ABC$ lie on one circle.

cz.2006.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all triples of pairwise distinct primes $p$, $q$, $r$ satisfying the following conditions: $$\begin{aligned}p&\mid q+r,\\q&\mid r+2p,\\r&\mid p+3q.\end{aligned}$$

cz.2006.2.6.reviewed_statement: Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}\tan^2 x+2\cot^2 2y&=1,\\\tan^2 y+2\cot^2 2z&=1,\\\tan^2 z+2\cot^2 2x&=1.\end{aligned}$$

cz.2007.1.1.reviewed_statement: A piece is placed on some square of an $n\times n$ chessboard ($n\ge 2$) and is then moved alternately “diagonally” and “straight”. “Diagonally” means to a square that has exactly one point in common with the previous one. “Straight” means to an adjacent square that has a common side with the previous one. Determine all $n$ for which there exist a starting square and a sequence of moves beginning with a “diagonal” move such that the piece passes through the whole chessboard and visits every square exactly once.

cz.2007.1.2.reviewed_statement: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $L$, $M$ be the incentres of the triangles $BCA$, $BCD$, respectively. Further, let $R$ be the intersection of the perpendiculars drawn from the points $L$ and $M$ to the lines $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. Prove that the triangle $LMR$ is isosceles.

cz.2007.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the set of all positive integers and consider all functions $f\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for arbitrary $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$ $$f\bigl(xf(y)\bigr)=yf(x).$$ Determine the smallest possible value of $f(2007)$.
cz.2007.1.3.rationale: Natural-number functional equation and its smallest value.

cz.2007.2.4.reviewed_statement: A set $M$ contains all positive integers from $1$ to $2007$ inclusive and has the following property: if a number $n$ is an element of the set $M$, then all terms of the arithmetic progression with first term $n$ and common difference $n+1$ lie in $M$. Decide whether the set $M$ must contain all positive integers greater than some number $m$.
cz.2007.2.4.rationale: Set closed under arithmetic progressions covering a tail of natural numbers.

cz.2007.2.5.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ with $|AC|\ne|BC|$ is given. Consider points $D$ and $E$ in the interiors of its sides $BC$ and $AC$, respectively, for which $ABDE$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. Let $P$ be the intersection of its diagonals $AD$ and $BE$. Prove that if the lines $CP$ and $AB$ are perpendicular, then $P$ is the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$.

cz.2007.2.6.reviewed_statement: Determine all ordered triples $(x,y,z)$ of pairwise distinct real numbers which satisfy the set equation $$\{x,y,z\}=\left\{\frac{x-y}{y-z},\ \frac{y-z}{z-x},\ \frac{z-x}{x-y}\right\}.$$

cz.2008.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine the coefficients $p$, $q$, $r$ of the polynomial $f(x)=x^3+px^2+qx+r$ if you know that they are nonzero pairwise distinct integers and that $f(p)=p^3$, $f(q)=q^3$.
cz.2008.1.1.rationale: Integer coefficients of a cubic evaluated at its coefficients.

cz.2008.1.2.reviewed_statement:
In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $|AC|\ne|BC|$, let $D$ and $E$ be the feet of the altitudes from the vertices $A$ and $B$. Let $V$ be the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$, $F$ the intersection of the lines $AB$ and $DE$, and $S$ the midpoint of the side $AB$. Further, let $K$ be the intersection of the circumcircles of the triangles $BDS$ and $AES$ different from the point $S$.

a) Prove that the points $D$, $E$, $V$, $K$ lie on one circle.

b) Prove that the points $F$, $V$, $K$ lie on one line.

cz.2008.1.3.reviewed_statement: In an $n\times n$ table, where $n\ge 2$, all the numbers $1,2,\dots,n^2$ are written row by row in this order (the first row contains the numbers $1,2,\dots,n$ in succession, the second row $n+1,n+2,\dots,2n$, etc.). In one step we may choose any two numbers in adjacent cells (i.e. cells having a common side) and either increase both of them by $1$ or decrease both of them by $1$. For which $n$ is it possible to obtain, after a finite number of steps, a table in which all numbers are equal to $365$?
cz.2008.1.3.rationale: Integer grid operations, linear invariants and reachability of equal entries.

cz.2008.2.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that for no positive integer $n$ is the number $27^n-n^{27}$ a prime.

cz.2008.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers whose product is $1$. Prove that if $k$, $m$ are positive integers with $k>m$, then $$x^k+y^k+z^k\ge x^m+y^m+z^m.$$

cz.2009.1.1.reviewed_statement: Prove that if all of the numbers $p$, $3p+2$, $5p+4$, $7p+6$, $9p+8$ and $11p+10$ are primes, then the number $6p+11$ is composite.

cz.2009.1.2.reviewed_statement: On the shorter of the arcs $CD$ of the circumcircle of a rectangle $ABCD$, choose a point $P$. Denote by $K$, $L$ and $M$ the feet of the perpendiculars from $P$ to the lines $AB$, $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. Show that the angle $LKM$ measures $45^\circ$ if and only if $ABCD$ is a square.

cz.2009.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest positive number $x$ with the following property: if $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ are arbitrary positive numbers whose product is $1$, then $$a^x+b^x+c^x+d^x\ge \frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}+\frac{1}{d}.$$

cz.2009.2.4.reviewed_statement:
We investigate for which positive integers $n$ there exist exactly four positive integers $k$ such that the number $n+k$ is a divisor of the number $n+k^2$.

a) Show that $n=58$ has this property and find the corresponding four numbers $k$.

b) Prove that an even number $n=2p$, where $p\ge 3$, has this property if and only if both $p$ and $2p+1$ are primes.

(Zero is not counted among the natural numbers.)

cz.2009.2.5.reviewed_statement: At each vertex of a regular $n$-gon $A_1A_2\dots A_n$ there lies a certain number of coins: at the vertex $A_k$ there are exactly $k$ coins, $1\le k\le n$. We choose two coins and move each of them to a neighbouring vertex in such a way that one of them moves clockwise and the other one counterclockwise. Decide for which $n$ it is possible, after a finite number of such moves, to achieve that for every $k$, $1\le k\le n$, there are $n+1-k$ coins at the vertex $A_k$.
cz.2009.2.5.rationale: Cyclic coin transfers and modular reachability.

cz.2009.2.6.reviewed_statement: Two distinct points $O$ and $T$ are given in a plane $\omega$. Find the set of vertices of all triangles which lie in the plane $\omega$ and have centroid at the point $T$ and circumcentre at the point $O$.

cz.2010.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine all pairs of positive integers $a$, $b$ such that $$4^a+4a^2+4=b^2.$$

cz.2010.1.2.reviewed_statement: A circular target of radius $12\,\mathrm{cm}$ has been hit by $19$ shots. Prove that the distance between some two of the hits is less than $7\,\mathrm{cm}$.
cz.2010.1.2.rationale: Packing points in a circular disk and a close pair.

cz.2010.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Rumburak kidnapped to his castle $31$ members of party $A$, $28$ members of party $B$, $23$ members of party $C$ and $19$ members of party $D$, and locked each of them in a separate cell. After work they could occasionally walk in the courtyard and talk. As soon as three members of three different parties started talking together, Rumburak, as a punishment, re-registered them into the fourth party. (Never did more than three of the kidnapped talk together.)

a) Could it happen that after some time all the kidnapped were members of one party? Of which one?

b) Determine all quadruples of positive integers whose sum is $101$ and which, as the numbers of kidnapped members of the four parties, make it possible that, thanks to Rumburak, all of them eventually become members of one party.

cz.2010.2.4.reviewed_statement: A circle $k$ with a chord $AC$ which is not a diameter is given. On its tangent through the point $A$ we choose a point $X\ne A$ and denote by $D$ the intersection of the circle $k$ with the interior of the segment $XC$ (if it exists). We complete the triangle $ACD$ to a trapezoid $ABCD$ inscribed in the circle $k$. Determine the locus of the intersections of the lines $BC$ and $AD$ corresponding to all such trapezoids.

cz.2010.2.5.reviewed_statement: The numbers $1, 2, \dots, 33$ are written on a blackboard. In one step we choose two numbers written on the blackboard whose product is a perfect square, erase both chosen numbers and write the square root of their product on the blackboard. We continue in this way until only numbers remain on the blackboard such that the product of no two of them is a perfect square. (In one step we may also erase two equal numbers and replace them by the same number.) Prove that at least $16$ numbers remain on the blackboard.
cz.2010.2.5.rationale: Square-product replacement and a lower bound on surviving integers.

cz.2010.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find the minimum of the expression $$\frac{a+b+c}{2}-\frac{[a,b]+[b,c]+[c,a]}{a+b+c},$$ where the variables $a$, $b$, $c$ are arbitrary integers greater than $1$ and $[x,y]$ denotes the least common multiple of the numbers $x$, $y$.

cz.2011.1.2.reviewed_statement: Determine all triples of primes $(p,q,r)$ such that $$(p+1)(q+2)(r+3)=4pqr.$$

cz.2011.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Suppose that real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ satisfy the system of equations $$x+y+z=12,\qquad x^2+y^2+z^2=54.$$ Prove that then the following statements hold:

a) Each of the numbers $xy$, $yz$, $zx$ is at least $9$ but at most $25$.

b) One of the numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ is at most $3$ and another one of them is at least $5$.

cz.2011.2.4.reviewed_statement: Consider a quadratic trinomial $ax^2+bx+c$ with real coefficients $a\ge 2$, $b\ge 2$, $c\ge 2$. Adam and Boris play the following game: when it is Adam's turn, he chooses one of the coefficients of the trinomial and replaces it by the *sum* of the other two. When it is Boris's turn, he chooses one of the coefficients and replaces it by the *product* of the other two. Adam starts and the players alternate regularly. The winner is the player after whose move the resulting trinomial has two distinct real roots. Depending on the coefficients $a$, $b$, $c$ of the initial trinomial, determine which of the players has a winning strategy.
cz.2011.2.4.rationale: Coefficient-update game on a real quadratic.

cz.2011.2.5.reviewed_statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$ which is not equilateral, denote by $P$ the foot of the altitude from the vertex $C$ to the side $AB$, by $V$ the orthocenter, by $O$ the circumcentre, by $D$ the intersection of the ray $CO$ with the side $AB$ and by $E$ the midpoint of the segment $CD$. Prove that the line $EP$ passes through the midpoint of the segment $OV$.

cz.2011.2.6.reviewed_statement: Denote by $\mathbb{R}^+$ the set of all positive real numbers. Determine all functions $f\colon \mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ such that for all $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^+$ $$f(x)\cdot f(y)=f(y)\cdot f\bigl(x\cdot f(y)\bigr)+\frac{1}{xy}.$$

cz.2012.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find all integers $n$ for which $n^4-3n^2+9$ is a prime.

cz.2012.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find the largest possible area of a triangle $ABC$ whose medians have lengths satisfying the inequalities $t_a\le 2$, $t_b\le 3$, $t_c\le 4$.

cz.2012.1.3.reviewed_statement: Prove that among any $101$ real numbers there exist two numbers $u$ and $v$ such that $$100\,|u-v|\cdot|1-uv|\le (1+u^2)(1+v^2).$$
cz.2012.1.3.rationale: Close pair inequality among a finite real set.

cz.2012.2.4.reviewed_statement: A point $X$ is given in the interior of a parallelogram $ABCD$. Construct a line which passes through the point $X$ and divides the given parallelogram into two parts whose areas differ from each other as much as possible.

cz.2012.2.5.reviewed_statement: In a group of $90$ children, each child has at least $30$ friends (friendship is mutual). Prove that the children can be divided into three groups of $30$ in such a way that each child has at least one friend in its own group.

cz.2012.2.6.reviewed_statement: Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} x^4+y^2+4&=5yz,\\ y^4+z^2+4&=5zx,\\ z^4+x^2+4&=5xy. \end{aligned}$$

cz.2013.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs of integers $a$, $b$ for which the equality $$\frac{a^2+1}{2b^2-3}=\frac{a-1}{2b-1}$$ holds.

cz.2013.1.2.reviewed_statement: Each of the robbers in a band of $n$ members ($n\ge 3$) has plundered a certain number of coins. Altogether $100n$ coins were plundered. The robbers decided to share the loot in the following way: in each step, one of the robbers gives one coin to each of two other robbers. Find all positive integers $n\ge 3$ for which, after a finite number of steps, each robber can have $100$ coins, regardless of how many coins the individual robbers plundered.
cz.2013.1.2.rationale: Coin redistribution with congruence and reachability constraints.

cz.2013.1.3.reviewed_statement: In a parallelogram $ABCD$ with centre $S$, denote by $O$ the centre of the incircle of the triangle $ABD$ and by $T$ its point of tangency with the diagonal $BD$. Prove that the lines $OS$ and $CT$ are parallel.

cz.2013.2.4.reviewed_statement: A positive integer $N$ is written on a blackboard in the decimal system. If it is not a one-digit number, we erase its last digit $c$ and replace the number $m$ which remains on the blackboard by the number $|m-3c|$. (For example, if the number $N=1204$ was on the blackboard, after the operation there will be $120-3\cdot 4=108$.) Find all positive integers $N$ from which, by repeating the described operation, we eventually obtain the number $0$.

cz.2013.2.5.reviewed_statement: A parallelogram $ABCD$ is given such that the feet $K$, $L$ of the perpendiculars dropped from the point $D$ to the sides $AB$, $BC$, respectively, are interior points of these sides. Prove that $KL\parallel AC$ if and only if $$|\angle BCA|+|\angle ABD|=|\angle BDA|+|\angle ACD|.$$

cz.2013.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all positive real numbers $p$ such that $$\sqrt{a^2+pb^2}+\sqrt{b^2+pa^2}\ge a+b+(p-1)\sqrt{ab}$$ holds for every pair of positive real numbers $a$, $b$.

cz.2014.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Denote all its positive divisors by $d_1, d_2, \dots, d_k$ so that $d_1<d_2<\dots<d_k$ (i.e. $d_1=1$ and $d_k=n$). Determine all values of $n$ for which $d_5-d_3=50$ and $11d_5+8d_7=3n$.

cz.2014.1.2.reviewed_statement: In a plane in which a segment $AB$ is given, consider triangles $XYZ$ such that $X$ is an interior point of the segment $AB$, the triangles $XBY$ and $XZA$ are similar ($\triangle XBY\sim\triangle XZA$), and the points $A$, $B$, $Y$, $Z$ lie on a circle in this order. Find the locus of the midpoints of all the segments $YZ$.

cz.2014.2.4.reviewed_statement: $234$ spectators came to a cinema. Determine for which $n\ge 4$ it could happen that the spectators could be seated in $n$ rows so that each spectator in the $i$-th row knew exactly $j$ spectators in the $j$-th row, for any $i, j\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, $i\ne j$. (The relation of acquaintance is mutual.)
cz.2014.2.4.rationale: Integer class sizes with prescribed bipartite degrees.

cz.2014.2.5.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. Denote by $k$ the circle with diameter $AB$. The circle which touches the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ at the point $A$ and passes through the point $C$ intersects the circle $k$ at a point $P$, $P\ne A$. The circle which touches the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ at the point $B$ and passes through the point $C$ intersects the circle $k$ at a point $Q$, $Q\ne B$. Prove that the intersection of the lines $AQ$ and $BP$ lies on the angle bisector of $\angle ACB$.

cz.2014.2.6.reviewed_statement: Prove that for any non-negative real numbers $a$ and $b$ the inequality $$\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2+1}}+\frac{b}{\sqrt{a^2+1}}\ge\frac{a+b}{\sqrt{ab+1}}$$ holds, and determine when equality occurs.

cz.2015.1.2.reviewed_statement:
For a given positive integer $n$, determine the number of paths of length $2n+2$ from the point $[0,0]$ to the point $[n,n]$ which do not pass through any point more than once. By a path of length $2n+2$ from the point $[0,0]$ to the point $[n,n]$ we mean a $(2n+2)$-term sequence $$(A_0A_1, A_1A_2, A_2A_3, \dots, A_{2n+1}A_{2n+2})$$ of segments joining two neighbouring lattice points, where $A_0=[0,0]$, $A_{2n+2}=[n,n]$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/czsk_2015_p2_fig.png
cz.2015.1.2.rationale: Counting self-avoiding lattice paths of prescribed length.

cz.2015.1.3.reviewed_statement: In an arbitrary triangle $ABC$ in which the median from the vertex $C$ is perpendicular neither to the side $CA$ nor to the side $CB$, denote by $X$ and $Y$ the intersections of the perpendicular bisector of this median with the lines $CA$ and $CB$. Find all such triangles $ABC$ for which the points $A$, $B$, $X$, $Y$ lie on a circle.

cz.2015.2.4.reviewed_statement: Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} a(b^2+c)&=c(c+ab),\\ b(c^2+a)&=a(a+bc),\\ c(a^2+b)&=b(b+ca). \end{aligned}$$

cz.2015.2.5.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ is given in which any two sides differ in length by at least $d>0$. Denote by $T$ its centroid, by $I$ the centre of its incircle and by $\varrho$ the radius of the incircle. Prove that $$S_{AIT}+S_{BIT}+S_{CIT}\ge\frac{2}{3}d\varrho,$$ where $S_{XYZ}$ denotes the area of the triangle $XYZ$.

cz.2015.2.6.reviewed_statement: A positive integer $n>2$ is given. Determine the largest integer $d$ for which the following statement holds: from any $n$-element set of integers one can choose three distinct non-empty subsets such that the sum of the elements of each of them is an integer multiple of the number $d$. (The chosen subsets may have common elements.)
cz.2015.2.6.rationale: Three subset sums simultaneously divisible by a maximal modulus.

cz.2016.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $p>3$ be a given prime. Determine the number of all ordered six-tuples $(a,b,c,d,e,f)$ of positive integers whose sum equals $3p$ and such that all the fractions $$\frac{a+b}{c+d},\quad \frac{b+c}{d+e},\quad \frac{c+d}{e+f},\quad \frac{d+e}{f+a},\quad \frac{e+f}{a+b}$$ have integer values.
cz.2016.1.1.rationale: Counting integer six-tuples with integral adjacent ratios.

cz.2016.1.2.reviewed_statement: Denote by $r$ and $r_a$ the radii of the incircle and of the excircle opposite to the side $BC$ of a triangle $ABC$, respectively. Prove that if $$r+r_a=|BC|,$$ then the triangle $ABC$ is right-angled.

cz.2016.1.3.reviewed_statement: Mathematical clubs are popular among the inhabitants of a certain town. Any two of the clubs have at least one common member. Prove that we can distribute compasses and rulers to the inhabitants of the town in such a way that only one inhabitant gets both, and yet each club, at full attendance of its members, has at its disposal both a ruler and a compass.
cz.2016.1.3.rationale: Two-resource allocation to intersecting set families.

cz.2016.2.4.reviewed_statement: Positive numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy $$(a+c)(b^2+ac)=4a.$$ Determine the maximum value of the expression $b+c$ and find all triples of numbers $(a,b,c)$ for which the expression attains this value.

cz.2016.2.5.reviewed_statement: In a triangle $ABC$ we have $|BC|=1$ and, moreover, there exists exactly one point $D$ on the side $BC$ such that $|DA|^2=|DB|\cdot|DC|$. Determine all possible values of the perimeter of the triangle $ABC$.

cz.2016.2.6.reviewed_statement: A piece called a prince is placed on some square of a $6\times 6$ chessboard. In one move it can jump either vertically or horizontally. The length of the jump is alternately one and two squares, the piece starting with a jump of length one (i.e. to a neighbouring square). Decide whether the starting position of the piece can be chosen so that, after a suitable sequence of $35$ jumps, it visits every square of the chessboard exactly once.

cz.2017.1.1.reviewed_statement: There are $100$ diamonds in a pile, of which $50$ are genuine and $50$ are fake. We invited a peculiar expert, the only one who can tell which are which. Every time we show him some three diamonds, he chooses two of them and (truthfully) tells us how many of these two are genuine. Decide whether we can surely identify all the genuine diamonds, regardless of how the expert chooses the pairs to be assessed.

cz.2017.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x$, $y$ $$f(y-xy)=f(x)y+(x-1)^2f(y).$$

cz.2017.2.4.reviewed_statement: To each sequence consisting of $n$ zeros and $n$ ones we assign the number of blocks of equal digits in it. (For example, the sequence $00111001$ has $4$ such blocks: $00$, $111$, $00$, $1$.) For a given $n$ we add up all the numbers assigned to all such sequences. Prove that the resulting sum equals $$(n+1)\binom{2n}{n}.$$
cz.2017.2.4.rationale: Total block counts in balanced binary strings.

cz.2017.2.5.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ with orthocenter $H$ is given. The angle bisector of $\angle BHC$ intersects the side $BC$ at a point $D$. Denote by $E$ and $F$ the images of the point $D$ under the reflections in the lines $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircle of the triangle $AEF$ passes through the midpoint of the arc $BAC$.

cz.2017.2.6.reviewed_statement: A non-zero integer $k$ is given. Prove that the equation $$k=\frac{x^2-xy+2y^2}{x+y}$$ is satisfied by an odd number of ordered pairs of integers $(x,y)$ if and only if $k$ is divisible by seven.
cz.2017.2.6.rationale: Parity of integer solution counts governed by divisibility by seven.

cz.2018.1.1.reviewed_statement: In a group of people, some pairs are friends. For a positive integer $k\ge 3$ we say that the group is $k$-good if every $k$-tuple of people from the group can be seated around a round table so that every two neighbours are friends. Prove that if the group is $6$-good, then it is also $7$-good.

cz.2018.1.3.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ is given. The angle bisector at vertex $A$ meets side $BC$ at point $D$. Let $E$, $F$ be the circumcentres of triangles $ABD$, $ACD$, respectively. What can the measure of angle $BAC$ be if the circumcentre of triangle $AEF$ lies on the line $BC$?

cz.2018.2.5.reviewed_statement: An isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$ with the longer base $AB$ is given. Let $I$ be the incentre of triangle $ABC$ and $J$ the centre of the excircle of triangle $ACD$ opposite to side $AD$. Prove that the lines $IJ$ and $AB$ are parallel.

cz.2018.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest positive integer $n$ such that for any colouring of the numbers $1, 2, 3, \dots, n$ with three colours there exist two numbers of the same colour among them whose difference is the square of a positive integer.
cz.2018.2.6.rationale: Three-colouring an integer interval with square-distance restrictions.

cz.2019.1.1.reviewed_statement: Solve the system of equations in the set of real numbers: $$\begin{aligned} x^2-yz&=|y-z|+1,\\ y^2-zx&=|z-x|+1,\\ z^2-xy&=|x-y|+1.\end{aligned}$$

cz.2019.1.2.reviewed_statement: A rectangle $ABCD$ with $|AB|=a\ge b=|BC|$ is given. Construct points $P$ and $Q$ on the line $BD$ such that $|AP|=|PQ|=|QC|$. Discuss the solvability of the problem with respect to the lengths $a$, $b$.

cz.2019.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $n$ be positive integers such that the following conditions hold:
(i) the numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $a+b+c$ are pairwise coprime;
(ii) the number $(a+b+c)(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)(ab+bc+ca)$ is the $n$-th power of an integer.
Prove that the product $abc$ can be written as the difference of two $n$-th powers of integers.

cz.2019.2.4.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. On the ray opposite to the ray $BC$ lies a point $P$ such that $|AB|=|BP|$. Analogously, on the ray opposite to the ray $CB$ lies a point $Q$ such that $|AC|=|CQ|$. Let $J$ be the centre of the excircle of the triangle opposite to side $BC$, and let $D$, $E$ be its points of tangency with the lines $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Suppose that the rays opposite to the rays $DP$ and $EQ$ intersect at a point $F$ different from $J$. Prove that $AF\perp FJ$.

cz.2019.2.6.reviewed_statement: For which positive integers $n$ is it possible to write all the integers from $1$ to $n^2$ into an $n\times n$ table so that the arithmetic mean of the numbers in every row and in every column of the table is an integer?
cz.2019.2.6.rationale: Integer row and column means in a number array.

cz.2020.1.1.reviewed_statement: Two positive integers $m$ and $n$ are written on a board. In each step, we replace one of the two numbers on the board by either their sum, or their product, or their quotient (if it is an integer). Depending on the numbers $m$ and $n$, determine all pairs that can appear on the board after several steps.
cz.2020.1.1.rationale: Reachable integer pairs under sum, product and integral quotient moves.

cz.2020.1.2.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ is given. Points $X$ and $Y$ are chosen in the interiors of its sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Let $Z$ be the intersection of the segments $BY$ and $CX$. Prove the inequality $$[BZX]+[CZY]>2[XYZ],$$ where $[DEF]$ denotes the area of triangle $DEF$.

cz.2020.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Consider the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} x^2-3y+p&=z,\\ y^2-3z+p&=x,\\ z^2-3x+p&=y\end{aligned}$$ with a real parameter $p$.
a) For $p\ge 4$, solve the system in the set of real numbers.
b) Prove that for $p\in[1,4)$ every real solution of the system satisfies $x=y=z$.

cz.2020.2.4.reviewed_statement: Positive integers $a$, $b$ satisfy the equality $b^2=a^2+ab+b$. Prove that $b$ is the square of a positive integer.

cz.2020.2.5.reviewed_statement: An isosceles triangle $ABC$ with base $BC$ is given, and a point $D$ is chosen in the interior of the base. Let $E$, $F$ be points on the sides $AB$, $AC$, respectively, such that $\angle BED=\angle DFC>90^\circ$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $ABF$ and $AEC$ intersect on the line $AD$ at a point different from $A$.

cz.2020.2.6.reviewed_statement:
For every positive integer $k$, let $P(k)$ denote the number of all positive $4k$-digit integers which can be formed from the digits $2$, $0$ and which are divisible by $2\,020$. Prove the inequality $$P(k)\ge \binom{2k-1}{k}^2$$ and determine all $k$ for which equality holds.
(Note. The decimal representation of a positive integer cannot begin with the digit $0$.)
cz.2020.2.6.rationale: Counting digit-constrained integers divisible by a fixed modulus.

cz.2021.1.1.reviewed_statement: A fraction with $1010$ boxes in the numerator and $1011$ boxes in the denominator serves as the game board for a two-player game: $$\frac{\square+\square+\dots+\square}{\square+\square+\dots+\square+\square}$$ The players alternate in turns. In each turn, a player chooses one of the numbers $1, 2, \dots, 2021$ and places it into any empty box. Each number may be used only once. The starting player wins if, after all the boxes are filled, the value of the fraction differs from the number $1$ by less than $10^{-6}$. Otherwise the second player wins. Decide which of the players has a winning strategy.
cz.2021.1.1.rationale: Number-placement game with a rational-value target.

cz.2021.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $I$ be the incentre of a right triangle $ABC$ with the right angle at vertex $A$. Further, let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the segments $AB$ and $BI$. Prove that the line $CI$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $BMN$.

cz.2021.1.3.reviewed_statement: Pairwise distinct non-zero real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy the set equality $$\{a+b,\,b+c,\,c+a\}=\{ab,\,bc,\,ca\}.$$ Prove that the equality $$\{a,\,b,\,c\}=\{a^2-2,\,b^2-2,\,c^2-2\}$$ also holds.

cz.2021.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ for which the equality $$n+d(n)+d(d(n))+\dots=2021$$ holds, where $d(0)=d(1)=0$ and for $k>1$, $d(k)$ is the superdivisor of the number $k$ (i.e. its largest divisor $d$ with the property $d<k$).

cz.2021.2.5.reviewed_statement: We call a string of characters neat if it has even length and its first half is identical to its second half (e.g. $abab$). We call a string nice if it can be split into several neat strings (such as $abcabcdedeff$ into $abcabc$, $dede$ and $ff$). A reduction of a string is an operation in which we erase two equal adjacent characters from the string (e.g. the string $abbac$ can be reduced to $aac$ and that further to $c$). Prove that any string containing each of its characters an even number of times can be obtained by a series of reductions from a suitable nice string.

cz.2021.2.6.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. For each of its interior points $X$, let $X_a$, $X_b$, $X_c$ be its images under the reflections in the lines $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively. Prove that all the triangles $X_aX_bX_c$ have a common point.

cz.2022.1.1.reviewed_statement: $71$ non-zero real numbers are written in a row next to each other on a sheet of paper. Every number except the first and the last is $1$ less than the product of its two neighbours. Prove that the first and the last numbers are equal.
cz.2022.1.1.rationale: Finite multiplicative recurrence and equal endpoints.

cz.2022.1.2.reviewed_statement:
We say that a positive integer $d$ is fair if the number of $2021$-digit palindromes which are multiples of $d$ is the same as the number of $2022$-digit palindromes which are multiples of $d$. Does the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 35\}$ contain more numbers that are fair, or more that are not fair?
(A palindrome is a positive integer whose decimal representation reads the same from left to right as from right to left.)
cz.2022.1.2.rationale: Counting divisible palindromes of two lengths.

cz.2022.1.3.reviewed_statement: In an acute scalene triangle $ABC$, let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$ and $N$ the midpoint of the arc $BAC$ of its circumcircle. Further, let $l$ be the circle with diameter $BC$ and let $D$, $E$ be the intersections of $l$ with the bisector of angle $BAC$. Points $F$, $G$ lie on the circle $l$ so that the quadrilateral $DEFG$ is a rectangle. Prove that the points $F$, $G$, $M$, $N$ lie on a circle.

cz.2022.2.4.reviewed_statement: In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ we have $|AB|=|BC|=|CD|$. Let $P$ be the intersection of its diagonals and let $O$, $Q$ be the circumcentres of triangles $APB$ and $DPC$, respectively. Prove that the quadrilateral $OBCQ$ is a parallelogram.

cz.2022.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all integers $n$ for which the number $$2^n+n^2$$ is the square of some integer.

cz.2023.1.1.reviewed_statement: Alica and Bohuš play a game on a board with $72$ cells arranged around the circumference of a circle. At the beginning, Bohuš places one token on each of some of the cells. In each round, Alica first chooses an empty cell and Bohuš must then move a token onto it from one of the adjacent cells. If he cannot do so, the game ends; otherwise the next round follows. Determine the smallest number of tokens for which Bohuš can ensure that the game lasts at least $2023$ rounds.
cz.2023.1.1.rationale: Defensive token movement game on a cycle.

cz.2023.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be an integer with $n\ge 3$ and let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be the side lengths of an arbitrary $n$-gon. Prove the inequality $$a_1+a_2+\dots+a_n>\sqrt{2\left(a_1^2+a_2^2+\dots+a_n^2\right)}.$$

cz.2023.1.3.reviewed_statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $H$ be its orthocenter and $I$ its incentre. Let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $I$ to the line $BC$ and let $E$ be the image of point $A$ under the point reflection with centre $I$. Further, let $F$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $H$ to the line $ED$. Prove that the points $B$, $H$, $F$ and $C$ lie on a circle.

cz.2023.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Let $(a_n)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that for $n\ge 0$, $$a_{n+2}=a_0a_1+a_1a_2+\dots+a_na_{n+1}-1.$$
a) Prove that some prime divides infinitely many terms of this sequence.
b) Prove that there are infinitely many such primes.
cz.2023.2.4.rationale: Prime divisors of an integer sum-product recurrence.

cz.2023.2.5.reviewed_statement: In a triangle $ABC$, let $M$, $N$, $P$ be the midpoints of the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively, and $G$ its centroid. Let the circumcircle of triangle $BGP$ meet the line $MP$ at a point $K$ different from $P$, and let the circumcircle of triangle $CGN$ meet the line $MN$ at a point $L$ different from $N$. Prove that $\angle BAK=\angle CAL$.

cz.2023.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer with $n\ge 3$. Consider an $n\times n$ square grid whose individual unit squares can be either white or black. In each step, we change the colours of five squares forming the shape shown below, in any rotation. At the beginning all squares are white. Decide for which $n$ it is possible, after a finite number of steps, to make all the squares black.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/czsk_2023_p6_fig.png
cz.2023.2.6.rationale: Binary grid flips by a prescribed pentomino shape.

cz.2024.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be positive integers such that one of the values $$\gcd(a,b)\cdot\operatorname{lcm}(b,c),\qquad \gcd(b,c)\cdot\operatorname{lcm}(c,a),\qquad \gcd(c,a)\cdot\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$$ is equal to the product of the remaining two. Prove that one of the numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ is a multiple of another one of them.
($\gcd(x,y)$ and $\operatorname{lcm}(x,y)$ denote the greatest common divisor and the least common multiple, respectively, of positive integers $x$, $y$.)

cz.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let an interior point $P$ of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ be such that $$\angle PAD=\angle ADP=\angle CBP=\angle PCB=\angle CPD.$$ Let $O$ be the circumcentre of triangle $CPD$. Prove that $|OA|=|OB|$.

cz.2024.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Determine the largest positive integer $n$ such that any set of $n$ tetrominoes, each of which has one of the four shapes in the figure, can be placed without overlapping into a $20\times 20$ table so that each tetromino covers exactly four cells of the table. The individual tetrominoes may be rotated and reflected arbitrarily.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/czsk_2024_p3_fig.png

cz.2024.2.4.reviewed_statement: $10$ boys and $10$ girls met at a party. Each boy likes a different positive number of girls. Each girl likes a different positive number of boys. Determine the largest non-negative integer $n$ such that it is always possible to form at least $n$ disjoint pairs in which each of the two likes the other.

cz.2024.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $(a_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of real numbers such that for every non-negative integer $k$, $$a_{k+1}=3a_k-\lfloor 2a_k\rfloor-\lfloor a_k\rfloor.$$ Determine all positive integers $n$ such that if $a_0=1/n$, then this sequence is constant from some term on.
(By $\lfloor x\rfloor$ we mean the greatest integer not exceeding the number $x$.)
cz.2024.2.5.rationale: Floor recurrence starting at reciprocal integers.

cz.2025.1.1.reviewed_statement: Real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ satisfy $$a+b+c+d=0$$ and $$\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c+\frac1d=0.$$ How many of the equalities $$\begin{aligned} ab&=cd,\\ ac&=bd,\\ ad&=bc\end{aligned}$$ can hold simultaneously?

cz.2025.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find the largest integer $n$ with the following property: Whenever five pairwise distinct points are given in the plane such that two of them lie in the interior of the triangle formed by the remaining three points, it is possible to label some three of these five points $X$, $Y$, $Z$ so that $n^\circ<\angle XYZ\le 180^\circ$.
cz.2025.1.2.rationale: Large angle forced by a five-point planar configuration.

cz.2025.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be the largest prime dividing a positive integer $n$, where $n>1$. For every non-empty subset of the divisors of $n$ we write down the sum of its elements. Suppose that in this way we have written down more than $p$ numbers from the set $\{1, 2, \dots, p+2\}$ and that no number from this set has been written down more than once. Prove that no number has been written down more than once.
cz.2025.1.3.rationale: Uniqueness of divisor subset sums from their initial range.

cz.2025.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ with the following property: In an $n\times n$ square table it is possible to colour $2n$ cells so that no two of them share a side or a vertex and every row and every column contains exactly $2$ coloured cells.

cz.2025.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $H$ be its orthocenter, $\omega$ its circumcircle and $O$ the centre of $\omega$. Further, let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$ and $D$ the intersection of the line $AH$ with the circle $\omega$ different from $A$. The line $DM$ meets the circle $\omega$ at a point $E$ different from $D$. Let $F$ be the intersection of the line $AE$ with the circumcircle of triangle $OME$ different from $E$. Prove that $|FH|=|FA|$.

cz.2026.1.1.reviewed_statement: Positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ satisfy $x^2+y^2+z^2=75$, and two of the three sums $x+y$, $y+z$, $z+x$ are at least $10$. Determine the smallest and the largest possible value of the remaining sum.

cz.2026.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle and let $T$ be its centroid. Let $P$ be a point of the shorter arc with endpoints $B$ and $C$ of the circumcircle of $ABC$, and let $Q$ be the foot of the perpendicular from point $P$ to the segment $BC$. Let $X$ be the intersection of the line $QT$ with the line through $A$ parallel to $BC$, and let $S$ be the midpoint of the segment $PX$. Prove that $\angle BAP=\angle SAC$.

cz.2026.1.3.reviewed_statement: We say that a group of people is tri-acquainted if each of its members knows exactly three other members and the group cannot be split into two non-empty parts so that every member has all of their acquaintances in their own part. (Acquaintance is mutual.) Determine the largest positive integer $k$ such that $k\ge 3$ and there exists a positive integer $n$ such that from every tri-acquainted group with at least $n$ people one can choose at least $k$ people and seat them around a round table so that every two neighbours know each other.

cz.2026.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct positive integers such that the numbers $a^2+1$ and $ab+1$ have the same sets of prime divisors. Prove that the number $a^2+b^2+2$ is divisible by the square of some prime.

cz.2026.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $\{a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2026}\}=\{1, 2, \dots, 2026\}$ and let $a_{i+2026}=a_i$ for every positive integer $i$. Determine the smallest possible and the largest possible number of indices $i$ from the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 2026\}$ such that each of the $2026$ numbers $$\begin{gathered} a_i,\\ a_i-a_{i+1},\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+a_{i+2},\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+a_{i+2}-a_{i+3},\\ \vdots\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+\dots-a_{i+2023}+a_{i+2024},\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+\dots-a_{i+2023}+a_{i+2024}-a_{i+2025}\end{gathered}$$ is non-negative.
cz.2026.2.5.rationale: Extremal number of nonnegative alternating prefix sums of cyclic permutations.

cz.2026.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCDEF$ be a hexagon inscribed in a circle with centre $O$ such that each two of its opposite sides are parallel. The lines $AB$, $CD$, $EF$ determine a triangle $\Delta_1$ and the lines $BC$, $DE$, $FA$ determine a triangle $\Delta_2$. Prove that the circumcentres of the triangles $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$ are symmetric with respect to the point $O$.

rs.2008.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Solve in integers the equation
$$12^x + y^4 = 2008^z.$$

rs.2008.1.2.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ is given. Let $D$ and $E$ be points on the line $AB$ such that $D - A - B - E$ (in this order), $AD = AC$ and $BE = BC$. The bisectors of the interior angles at the vertices $A$ and $B$ meet the opposite sides at the points $P$ and $Q$, respectively, and the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at the points $M$ and $N$, respectively. The line joining the point $A$ with the circumcentre of triangle $BME$ and the line joining the point $B$ with the circumcentre of triangle $AND$ meet at the point $X$. Prove that $CX \perp PQ$.

rs.2008.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Prove that for positive real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ with $a + b + c = 1$ the following inequality holds:
$$\frac{1}{bc + a + \frac{1}{a}} + \frac{1}{ca + b + \frac{1}{b}} + \frac{1}{ab + c + \frac{1}{c}} \le \frac{27}{31}.$$

rs.2008.2.4.rationale: Monochromatic triangle with prescribed circumradius and angle relation.

rs.2008.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let the sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be defined by $a_1 = 3$, $a_2 = 11$ and $a_n = 4a_{n-1} - a_{n-2}$ for $n \ge 3$. Prove that every term of this sequence is of the form $a^2 + 2b^2$ for some positive integers $a$ and $b$.
rs.2008.2.5.rationale: Integer linear recurrence with quadratic-form representations.

rs.2008.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCDE$ be a convex pentagon with $AB = 1$, $\angle BAE = \angle ABC = 120^\circ$, $\angle CDE = 60^\circ$ and $\angle ADB = 30^\circ$. Prove that the area of the pentagon $ABCDE$ is less than $\sqrt{3}$.

rs.2009.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the angles of a non-isosceles triangle $ABC$ at the vertices $A$ and $B$, respectively. Let the bisectors of these angles meet the opposite sides of the triangle at $D$ and $E$, respectively. Prove that the acute angle between the lines $DE$ and $AB$ is not greater than $\frac{|\alpha-\beta|}{3}$.

rs.2009.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest positive integer which is divisible by $2009$ and whose sum of digits equals $2009$.

rs.2009.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Find the largest positive integer $n$ for which there exist distinct sets $S_1, S_2, \dots, S_n$ such that:

$1^\circ$ $|S_i \cup S_j| \le 2004$ for any two $1 \le i, j \le n$, and

$2^\circ$ $S_i \cup S_j \cup S_k = \{1, 2, \dots, 2008\}$ for any three integers $1 \le i < j < k \le n$.
rs.2009.1.3.rationale: Extremal set family with union constraints.

rs.2009.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $A_n$ be the set of all permutations $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ of the set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for which
$$k \mid 2(a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_k) \quad \text{for all } 1 \le k \le n.$$
Find the number of elements of the set $A_n$.
rs.2009.2.4.rationale: Counting permutations with divisible prefix sums.

rs.2009.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $x, y, z$ be positive real numbers such that $xy + yz + zx = x + y + z$. Prove the inequality
$$\frac{1}{x^2+y+1} + \frac{1}{y^2+z+1} + \frac{1}{z^2+x+1} \le 1.$$
When does equality hold?

rs.2009.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $k$ be the incircle of a non-isosceles triangle $ABC$, with center $S$. The circle $k$ touches the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at the points $P$, $Q$, $R$, respectively. The line $QR$ meets the line $BC$ at the point $M$. A circle passing through $B$ and $C$ touches $k$ at the point $N$. The circumcircle of triangle $MNP$ meets the line $AP$ at a point $L$ different from $P$. Prove that the points $S$, $L$ and $M$ are collinear.

rs.2010.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Some of $n$ cities are connected by airline routes (all routes are two-way). There are exactly $m$ routes. Let $d_i$ be the number of routes leaving city $i$, for $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$. If $1 \le d_i \le 2010$ for every $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$, prove that
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} d_i^2 \le 4022m - 2010n.$$
Find all $n$ for which equality can be attained.

rs.2010.1.2.reviewed_statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$, $M$ is the midpoint of side $BC$, and $D$, $E$ and $F$ are the feet of the altitudes from $A$, $B$ and $C$, respectively. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, $S$ the midpoint of the segment $AH$, and $G$ the intersection of the segments $FE$ and $AH$. If $N$ is the intersection point of the median $AM$ and the circumcircle of triangle $BCH$, prove that $\angle HMA = \angle GNS$.

rs.2010.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Let $A$ be an infinite subset of the set of positive integers. Find all positive integers $n$ such that for every $a \in A$
$$a^n + a^{n-1} + \dots + a^1 + 1 \mid a^{n!} + a^{(n-1)!} + \dots + a^{1!} + 1.$$
rs.2010.1.3.rationale: Polynomial-value divisibility at infinitely many positive integers.

rs.2010.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. A line through $O$ meets the sides $CA$ and $CB$ at the points $D$ and $E$, respectively, and meets the circumcircle of triangle $ABO$ at a point $P$ (different from $O$) inside the triangle. A point $Q$ on the side $AB$ is such that $\frac{AQ}{QB} = \frac{DP}{PE}$. Prove that $\angle APQ = 2\angle CAP$.

rs.2010.2.5.reviewed_statement:
An $n \times n$ table whose cells contain the numbers $1, 2, \dots, n^2$ (each cell containing exactly one number and each number appearing in exactly one cell) is called a Niš table if all products of $n$ numbers located in $n$ “scattered” cells give the same remainder upon division by $n^2+1$. Does there exist a Niš table for:

(a) $n = 8$;

(b) $n = 10$?

($n$ cells are “scattered” if no two of them are in the same row or in the same column.)
rs.2010.2.5.rationale: Permutation arrays with transversal products constant modulo a fixed integer.

rs.2010.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $a_0$ and $a_n$ be distinct divisors of a positive integer $m$, and let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be a sequence of positive integers satisfying
$$a_{i+1} = |a_i \pm a_{i-1}| \quad \text{for } 0 < i < n.$$
If $\gcd(a_0, \dots, a_n) = 1$, prove that some term of the sequence is less than $\sqrt{m}$.
rs.2010.2.6.rationale: Integer signed recurrence and a gcd-based size bound.

rs.2011.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Let $n \ge 2$ be a positive integer and let the positive real numbers $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_n$ satisfy
$$(a_{k-1}+a_k)(a_k+a_{k+1}) = a_{k-1} - a_{k+1} \quad \text{for every } k = 1, 2, \dots, n-1.$$
Prove that $a_n < \frac{1}{n-1}$.

rs.2011.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be an odd positive integer such that both $\varphi(n)$ and $\varphi(n+1)$ are powers of two ($\varphi(n)$ is the number of positive integers not greater than $n$ and coprime to $n$). Prove that $n+1$ is a power of two or $n = 5$.

rs.2011.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $H$ be the orthocenter and $O$ the circumcenter of an acute triangle $ABC$. The points $D$ and $E$ are the feet of the altitudes from the vertices $A$ and $B$, respectively. Denote by $K$ the intersection point of the lines $OD$ and $BE$, and by $L$ the intersection point of the lines $OE$ and $AD$. Let $X$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $HKD$ and $HLE$, and $M$ the midpoint of side $AB$. Prove that the points $K$, $L$ and $M$ are collinear if and only if $X$ is the circumcenter of triangle $EOD$.

rs.2011.2.4.reviewed_statement: On the sides $AB$, $AC$ and $BC$ of a triangle $ABC$ the points $M$, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are given such that $AX = MX$ and $BY = MY$. Let $K$ and $L$ be the midpoints of the segments $AY$ and $BX$, respectively, and $O$ the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. If $O_1$ and $O_2$ are the reflections of $O$ with respect to $K$ and $L$, respectively, prove that the points $X$, $Y$, $O_1$ and $O_2$ lie on a circle.

rs.2011.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Do there exist positive integers $a$, $b$ and $c$, greater than $2011$, such that in decimal notation
$$\left(a + \sqrt{b}\right)^c = \dots 2010{,}2011\dots\ ?$$
(That is, the digits $2010$ immediately precede and the digits $2011$ immediately follow the decimal point.)

rs.2012.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Let $P$ be a point on the diagonal $BD$ of a parallelogram $ABCD$ such that $\angle PCB = \angle ACD$. The circumcircle of triangle $ABD$ meets the line $AC$ at the points $E$ and $A$. Prove that
$$\angle AED = \angle PEB.$$

rs.2012.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Find all positive integers $a$ and $b$ such that
$$a \mid b^2, \quad b \mid a^2 \quad \text{and} \quad a+1 \mid b^2+1.$$

rs.2012.1.3.reviewed_statement:
At some nodes of a $2012 \times 2012$ square grid there are a fly and $k$ spiders. One move consists of the following: the fly moves to an adjacent node or stays where it is, and after that each of the $k$ spiders moves to some adjacent node or stays where it is (several spiders may be at the same node). At every moment each spider and the fly know the positions of all the others.

a) Find the smallest $k$ such that the spiders can catch the fly in a finite number of moves, regardless of the initial positions of the fly and the spiders.

b) Answer the same question for the cubic grid $2012 \times 2012 \times 2012$.

(Two nodes are adjacent if they differ in exactly one coordinate, and by $1$ in that coordinate. A spider catches the fly if they are at the same node.)

rs.2012.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ for which there exists a permutation $(p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n)$ of $(1, 2, \dots, n)$ such that the sets $\{p_i + i \mid 1 \le i \le n\}$ and $\{p_i - i \mid 1 \le i \le n\}$ are complete residue systems modulo $n$.
rs.2012.2.4.rationale: Permutation whose sums and differences are complete residue systems.

rs.2013.1.1.reviewed_statement:
A positive integer $k$ is given. Let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a bijection such that for any two integers $i$ and $j$ with $|i-j| \le k$ we have $|f(i)-f(j)| \le k$. Prove that for all $i, j \in \mathbb{Z}$
$$|f(i)-f(j)| = |i-j|.$$
rs.2013.1.1.rationale: Bijection of integers preserving bounded distances is an isometry.

rs.2013.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Let
$$S_n = \left\{ \binom{n}{n}, \binom{2n}{n}, \binom{3n}{n}, \dots, \binom{n^2}{n} \right\}, \quad \text{for } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$
a) Prove that there exist infinitely many composite positive integers $n$ such that $S_n$ is not a complete residue system modulo $n$.

b) Prove that there exist infinitely many composite positive integers $n$ such that $S_n$ is a complete residue system modulo $n$.
rs.2013.1.2.rationale: Binomial coefficient residues modulo composite integers.

rs.2013.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Let $M$, $N$ and $P$ be the midpoints of the sides $BC$, $AC$ and $AB$, respectively, and $O$ the circumcenter of an acute triangle $ABC$. The circumcircles of triangles $BOC$ and $MNP$ meet at two distinct points $X$ and $Y$ inside the triangle $ABC$. Prove that
$$\angle BAX = \angle CAY.$$

rs.2013.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ for which it is possible to partition the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 3n\}$ into $n$ disjoint three-element subsets of the form $\{a, b, c\}$ in which $b-a$ and $c-b$ are distinct numbers from the set $\{n-1, n, n+1\}$.
rs.2013.2.4.rationale: Partition of an integer interval into triples with prescribed gaps.

rs.2013.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $A'$ and $B'$ be the feet of the altitudes from the vertices $A$ and $B$, respectively, of an acute triangle $ABC$ ($AC \neq BC$). A circle $k$ passes through the points $A'$ and $B'$ and touches the side $AB$ at the point $D$. If the triangles $ADA'$ and $BDB'$ have equal areas, prove that
$$\angle A'DB' = \angle ACB.$$

rs.2013.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Find the largest constant $K \in \mathbb{R}$ with the following property: if $a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 > 0$ are such that for all $i, j, k \in \mathbb{N}$, $1 \le i < j < k \le 4$, we have $a_i^2 + a_j^2 + a_k^2 \ge 2(a_ia_j + a_ja_k + a_ka_i)$, then
$$a_1^2 + a_2^2 + a_3^2 + a_4^2 \ge K(a_1a_2 + a_1a_3 + a_1a_4 + a_2a_3 + a_2a_4 + a_3a_4).$$

rs.2014.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$
$$f\big(xf(y) - yf(x)\big) = f(xy) - xy.$$

rs.2014.1.2.reviewed_statement: On the sides $BC$ and $AC$ of a triangle $ABC$ the points $D$ and $E$, respectively, are given. Let $F$ ($F \neq C$) be the intersection point of the circumcircle of triangle $CED$ and the line through $C$ parallel to $AB$. Let $G$ be the intersection point of the line $FD$ and the side $AB$, and let $H$ be the point on the line $AB$ such that $\angle HDA = \angle GEB$ and $A$ lies between $H$ and $B$. If $DG = EH$, prove that the intersection point of the segments $AD$ and $BE$ lies on the bisector of the angle $ACB$.

rs.2014.1.3.reviewed_statement: Two players play the following game. They alternately write down a positive integer greater than one, where it is not allowed to write a linear combination, with nonnegative integer coefficients, of previously written numbers. The player who cannot write a new number loses. Does one of the players have a winning strategy and, if so, which one?
rs.2014.1.3.rationale: Winning strategy in a game avoiding additive semigroup representations.

rs.2014.2.4.reviewed_statement: A positive integer $n$ is called crazy if and only if there exist positive integers $a > 1$ and $b > 1$ such that $n = a^b + b$. Do there exist $2014$ consecutive positive integers among which exactly $2012$ are crazy?
rs.2014.2.4.rationale: Consecutive integers representable by a power-plus-exponent form.

rs.2014.2.6.reviewed_statement: The bisectors of the interior angles at the vertices $A$ and $B$ of a triangle $ABC$ meet the opposite sides at the points $D$ and $E$, respectively. A rhombus is inscribed in the quadrilateral $ABDE$ so that each side of the quadrilateral contains exactly one vertex of the rhombus. If $\angle BAC = \alpha$ and $\angle ABC = \beta$, prove that at least one angle of the rhombus is not greater than $\max\{\alpha, \beta\}$.

rs.2016.1.2.reviewed_statement:
A positive integer $n$ is given. Define $f(0, j) = f(i, 0) = 0$, $f(1, 1) = n$ and
$$f(i, j) = \left\lfloor \frac{f(i-1, j)}{2} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{f(i, j-1)}{2} \right\rfloor$$
for all positive integers $i$ and $j$ with $(i, j) \neq (1, 1)$. How many ordered pairs of positive integers $(i, j)$ are there for which $f(i, j)$ is odd?
rs.2016.1.2.rationale: Two-dimensional floor recurrence and counting odd values.

rs.2016.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. A line $t$ touches the circumcircle of triangle $BOC$ and meets the sides $AB$ and $AC$ at the points $D$ and $E$, respectively ($D, E \neq A$). The point $A'$ is the reflection of $A$ in the line $t$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $A'DE$ and $ABC$ are tangent to each other.

rs.2016.2.4.reviewed_statement: In a triangle $ABC$ ($AB \neq AC$) the incircle, with center $I$, touches the side $BC$ at the point $D$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the segment $BC$. Prove that the perpendiculars from the points $M$ and $D$ to the lines $AI$ and $MI$, respectively, meet on the line containing the altitude of triangle $ABC$ from the vertex $A$.

rs.2016.2.5.reviewed_statement: There are given $2n-1$ two-element subsets of the set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. Prove that one can choose $n$ of these subsets whose union contains no more than $\frac{2}{3}n + 1$ elements.

rs.2016.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Positive integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2^{2016}}$ are given such that for all $n$, $1 \le n \le 2^{2016}$,
$$a_n \le 2016 \quad \text{and} \quad a_1a_2\cdots a_n + 1 \text{ is a perfect square.}$$
Prove that one of the numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2^{2016}}$ is equal to $1$.
rs.2016.2.6.rationale: Square prefix products and occurrence of the factor one.

rs.2017.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be positive real numbers with $a+b+c = 1$. Prove that
$$a\sqrt{2b+1} + b\sqrt{2c+1} + c\sqrt{2a+1} \le \sqrt{2 - (a^2+b^2+c^2)}.$$

rs.2017.1.2.reviewed_statement: A convex cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ is given. Let the lines $AD$ and $BC$ meet at the point $E$. On the sides $AD$ and $BC$ the points $M$ and $N$, respectively, are chosen such that $AM : MD = BN : NC$. The circumcircles of triangle $EMN$ and of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ meet at the points $X$ and $Y$. Prove that the lines $AB$, $CD$ and $XY$ are concurrent or all parallel.

rs.2017.1.3.reviewed_statement: There are $2n-1$ light bulbs in a row. Initially the middle one (the $n$-th) is on and all the others are off. In one step it is allowed to choose two non-adjacent bulbs that are off such that all bulbs between them are on, and to switch the state of these two bulbs as well as of all bulbs between them (for example, from the configuration $\bullet\circ\circ\circ\bullet$ one obtains $\circ\bullet\bullet\bullet\circ$). What is the largest possible number of steps that can be performed?

rs.2017.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ be a positive integer such that for every positive integer $n$ the number $n^2a - 1$ has at least one divisor greater than $1$ which leaves remainder $1$ upon division by $n$. Prove that $a$ is a perfect square.

rs.2017.2.5.reviewed_statement: Determine the largest number of queens that can be placed on a $2017 \times 2017$ board so that each queen attacks at most one of the other queens.

rs.2017.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $k$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, and $k_a$ the excircle opposite the vertex $A$. The two common tangents of the circles $k$ and $k_a$ meet the line $BC$ at the points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that $\angle PAB = \angle QAC$.

rs.2018.1.1.reviewed_statement: The incircle of triangle $ABC$ has center $I$ and touches the side $BC$ at the point $D$. On the segments $BI$ and $CI$ the points $P$ and $Q$, respectively, are chosen such that $\angle BAC = 2\angle PAQ$. Prove that $\angle PDQ = 90^\circ$.

rs.2018.1.2.reviewed_statement: A positive integer $n$, $n > 1$, is given. An integer $x$ is called beautiful if the remainder of $x^2$ upon division by $n$ is odd. Prove that there are no more than $1 + \lfloor \sqrt{3n} \rfloor$ consecutive beautiful positive integers.

rs.2018.1.3.reviewed_statement:
In the plane $n$ lines are given, no two of which are parallel and no three of which pass through a common point. By intersection points we mean all points at which some two of these lines intersect.

a) Prove that there exists a line such that on each of its sides there are at least
$$\left\lfloor \frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{10} \right\rfloor$$
intersection points (points lying on that line are not counted).

b) For which values of $n$ can equality be attained?
rs.2018.1.3.rationale: Balanced line cut of intersection points of a line arrangement.

rs.2018.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Prove that there exists exactly one polynomial $P(x)$ with real coefficients for which the polynomial
$$(x+y)^{1000} - P(x) - P(y)$$
is divisible by the polynomial $xy - x - y$.

rs.2018.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ and $b$ be odd positive integers greater than $1$. Consider an $a \times b$ board from which the cells $(2, 1)$, $(a-2, b)$ and $(a, b)$ are missing (by the cell $(i, j)$ we mean the cell at the intersection of row $i$ and column $j$). Suppose that this board is tiled with $2 \times 1$ dominoes and $2 \times 2$ squares (the dominoes may be rotated). Prove that at least $\frac{3}{2}(a+b) - 6$ dominoes were used.

rs.2018.2.6.reviewed_statement:
For a given positive integer $k$, let $n_k$ be the smallest positive integer such that there exists a finite set $A$ of integers with the following properties:

- for every $a \in A$ there exist $x, y \in A$ (not necessarily distinct) such that
$$n_k \mid a - x - y;$$
- there is no subset $B$ of $A$ with $|B| \le k$ and
$$n_k \mid \sum_{b \in B} b.$$

Prove that for all $k \ge 3$
$$n_k < \left(\frac{13}{8}\right)^{k+2}.$$
rs.2018.2.6.rationale: Additively closed residues and exclusion of short zero-sum subsets.

rs.2019.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$, $n > 1$, with the following property: if $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots, a_k$ are all the positive integers less than $n$ and coprime to $n$, ordered so that $a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < \dots < a_k$, then none of the sums $a_i + a_{i+1}$ for $i = 1, 2, \dots, k-1$ is divisible by $3$.

rs.2019.1.2.rationale: Embedding a finite real-step sequence in a bounded interval.

rs.2019.1.3.reviewed_statement: A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is circumscribed about a circle $k$. The lines $AD$ and $BC$ meet at the point $P$, and the circumcircles of triangles $PAB$ and $PCD$ meet at the point $X$. Prove that the tangents from $X$ to the circle $k$ make equal angles with the lines $AX$ and $CX$.

rs.2019.2.4.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ is given. Let $A_1$ be the reflection, with respect to the midpoint of side $BC$, of the intersection point of the bisector of $\angle BAC$ with the side $BC$. The points $B_1$ (on the side $CA$) and $C_1$ (on the side $AB$) are defined analogously. The intersection of the circumcircle of triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ with the line $AB$ is the set $\{Z, C_1\}$, with the line $BC$ the set $\{X, A_1\}$, and with the line $CA$ the set $\{Y, B_1\}$. If the perpendiculars from the points $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ to $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$, respectively, are concurrent, prove that triangle $ABC$ is isosceles.

rs.2019.2.5.reviewed_statement: On a spherical planet X there are $2n$ gas stations. Each station is paired with exactly one other station, and any two paired stations are located at diametrically opposite points of the planet. Each station holds a certain amount of gasoline. The following is known: if a car with an initially empty (sufficiently large) tank starts from any station, it can always reach the station paired with it (possibly refuelling at other stations along the way). Find all positive integers $n$ such that, for any arrangement of $2n$ stations satisfying the above condition, there always exists a station from which a car with an initially empty tank can start and visit all the other stations on the planet. (Assume that the car consumes a constant amount of gasoline per unit of distance.)
rs.2019.2.5.rationale: Fuel-constrained visiting routes on a sphere with antipodal station pairs.

rs.2019.2.6.reviewed_statement:
The sequences $(a_n)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ and $(b_n)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ are defined by the recurrence relations
$$a_0 = 0, \quad a_1 = 1, \quad a_{n+1} = \frac{2018}{n}a_n + a_{n-1} \quad \text{for } n \ge 1,$$
and
$$b_0 = 0, \quad b_1 = 1, \quad b_{n+1} = \frac{2020}{n}b_n + b_{n-1} \quad \text{for } n \ge 1.$$
Prove that
$$\frac{a_{1010}}{1010} = \frac{b_{1009}}{1009}.$$

rs.2022.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $k$ be the incircle of an acute triangle $ABC$, $AC \neq BC$, and $l$ its excircle touching the side $AB$. The line $p$ through the point $C$ perpendicular to $AB$ meets the circle $k$ at the points $X$ and $Y$, and the circle $l$ at the points $Z$ and $T$, where the points lie in the order $X - Y - Z - T$. A circle $m$ through the points $X$ and $Z$ meets the line $AB$ at the points $D$ and $E$. Prove that the points $D$, $Y$, $E$ and $T$ are concyclic.

rs.2022.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be positive real numbers with $a^3 + b^3 + c^3 = 3$. Prove the inequality
$$\frac{1}{3-2a} + \frac{1}{3-2b} + \frac{1}{3-2c} \ge 3.$$

rs.2022.1.3.reviewed_statement: An $n \times n$ table, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, is filled with the numbers from $1$ to $n^2$ in such a way that the difference of any two numbers in adjacent cells is at most $n$, and for every $k = 1, 2, \dots, n^2$ the set of cells containing the numbers $1, 2, \dots, k$ is connected, as is the set of cells containing the numbers $k, k+1, \dots, n^2$. Adjacent cells are cells sharing a common side, and a set of cells is called connected if from each of its cells one can reach every other cell of the set moving only through adjacent cells within the set. A pair of adjacent numbers, i.e. numbers located in adjacent cells, is called good if their absolute difference is exactly $n$ (one number may belong to several good pairs). Prove that the table contains at least $2(n-1)$ good pairs.

rs.2022.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Let $f(n)$ denote the number of numbers $x \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, for which $\gcd(x, n)$ is a prime or equal to $1$. Prove that
$$\sum_{d \mid n} f(d) + \varphi(n) \ge 2n.$$
For which $n$ does equality hold?

rs.2022.2.5.reviewed_statement: There are $n$ integers written on a board, $n \in \mathbb{N}$. In one move one may choose two equal numbers on the board and increase one of them by $1$ and decrease the other by $1$. Prove that in this game it is not possible to make more than $\frac{n^3}{6}$ moves.

rs.2022.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct primes and $\alpha$ a real number, $0 < \alpha < 3$. Prove that the sequence
$$\lfloor \alpha \rfloor, \lfloor 2\alpha \rfloor, \lfloor 3\alpha \rfloor, \dots$$
contains a term less than $2pq$ which is divisible by one of the numbers $p$ and $q$.
rs.2022.2.6.rationale: Floor multiples divisible by one of two primes.

rs.2023.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $O$ be the circumcenter of a scalene triangle $ABC$ and $H$ its orthocenter, $H \notin \{A, B, C\}$. Denote by $O_a$, $O_b$ and $O_c$ the circumcenters of triangles $AOH$, $BOH$ and $COH$, respectively. Prove that the lines $AO_a$, $BO_b$ and $CO_c$ are concurrent.

rs.2023.1.2.reviewed_statement: A cube with edge $2021$ is given. In how many different ways can one attach a single unit cube to the surface of this cube so that the resulting solid can be filled with blocks of dimensions $1 \times 1 \times k$, for some positive integer $k$, $k \ge 2$?
rs.2023.1.2.rationale: Counting placements of a unit cube permitting bar tilings.

rs.2023.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Suppose that positive integers $m$ and $n$ are given, as well as a sequence of integers $a_1, a_2, \dots$ such that $a_i = a_{i-n}$ for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, $i > n$. For every positive integer $j$, $1 \le j \le n$, define $l_j$ as the smallest positive integer such that the number $a_j + a_{j+1} + \dots + a_{j+l_j-1}$ is divisible by $m$. Prove that
$$l_1 + l_2 + \dots + l_n \le mn.$$
rs.2023.1.3.rationale: Cyclic partial sums and their shortest zero residues.

rs.2023.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $q$ be a prime and $n$ a positive integer. Prove that $n^q + \left(\frac{n-1}{2}\right)^2$ is not a perfect power of $q$.

rs.2023.2.5.rationale: Monotone real function fixed by Farey-mediant identities and its irrational value.

rs.2023.2.6.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$, $AB \neq AC$, with circumcircle $\omega$ is given. Let $I$ be the incenter of the triangle. The perpendicular to the line $AI$ through the point $I$ meets the sides $AB$ and $AC$ at the points $E$ and $F$, respectively. The circumcircle of triangle $AEF$ meets $\omega$ and the line $AI$ at the points $G$ and $H$, respectively. The point $D$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $I$ to the line $BC$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $G$ meets the line $BC$ at the point $J$, and the line $AJ$ meets the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ again at the point $K$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $DJK$ and $GIH$ are tangent to each other.

rs.2024.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $1 = d_1 < d_2 < d_3 < \dots < d_k = n$, where $k \ge 4$, be all the positive divisors of a given positive integer $n$. Find all positive integers $n$ for which there exists a permutation of the numbers $d_2 - d_1, d_3 - d_2, d_4 - d_3, \dots, d_k - d_{k-1}$ such that they form a finite geometric progression.
rs.2024.1.1.rationale: Permutation of consecutive divisor gaps into a geometric progression.

rs.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: A tournament of order $n$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, consists of $2^n$ players, indexed by the numbers from $1$ to $2^n$, and $n$ rounds. In each round the remaining players are paired up and compete in a mathematical duel, and the winner advances to the next round. The winner of the $n$-th round is considered the winner of the tournament. Two tournaments are considered different if there is a duel which took place in the $k$-th round of one tournament but not in the $k$-th round of the other, or if they have different winners. Determine how many different tournaments of order $n$ there are with the property that in every round the sums of the indices of the participants in each duel of that round are all equal.

rs.2024.1.3.reviewed_statement:
There are given $2n$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ and $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$. Prove that for every $m \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ there exist two real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$, $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 > 0$, such that $p_m = \min\{p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n\}$, where
$$p_j = \sum_{i=1}^{n} |\alpha(a_i - a_j) + \beta(b_i - b_j)|, \quad j \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}.$$

rs.2024.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let the points $I$ and $I_a$ be the incenter and the excenter opposite the vertex $A$, respectively, of a non-isosceles triangle $ABC$. The incircle of the triangle touches the sides $BC$, $AC$ and $AB$ at the points $D$, $E$ and $F$, respectively. The lines $EF$ and $BC$ meet at the point $P$, and the point $X$ is the midpoint of the segment $PD$. Prove that $XI \perp I_aD$.

rs.2024.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $n \ge 3$ be a fixed positive integer. Find all positive integers $k$ for which the function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by
$$f(x) = \cos^k x + \cos^k\left(x + \frac{2\pi}{n}\right) + \cos^k\left(x + \frac{4\pi}{n}\right) + \dots + \cos^k\left(x + \frac{2(n-1)\pi}{n}\right), \quad x \in \mathbb{R},$$
is constant.

rs.2024.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all nonconstant polynomials $P$ with integer coefficients and positive leading coefficient such that the number $P^{2mn}(m^2) + n^2$ is the square of an integer for all positive integers $m$ and $n$. (Here $P^k(x) = \underbrace{P(P(\dots P}_{k}(x)\dots))$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$.)
rs.2024.2.6.rationale: Iterated integer polynomial values always forming squares after a shift.

rs.2026.1.1.reviewed_statement:
What is the largest possible number of distinct remainders upon division by $2026$ that the elements of the set
$$\{\pi(1), 2\pi(2), 3\pi(3), \dots, 2026\pi(2026)\}$$
can give, where $\pi$ is an arbitrary permutation of the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 2026\}$?
rs.2026.1.1.rationale: Maximum distinct product residues generated by a permutation.

rs.2026.1.2.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ with $AB < AC$ is given. Let $D$ and $E$ be the feet of the altitudes from the vertices $A$ and $B$, respectively, $H$ the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $F$ be the intersection point of the bisector of the interior angle at the vertex $A$ with the line $BC$. The intersection of the lines $AF$ and $BE$ is the point $I$. If the circumcircles of triangles $BHC$ and $DFI$ meet at the points $M$ and $P$, prove that the quadrilateral $AEMP$ is cyclic.

rs.2026.1.3.reviewed_statement:
A regular $2n$-gon $A_1A_2\dots A_{2n}$, $n \ge 3$, is given, whose sides are colored with $n$ colors so that any two opposite sides have the same color. Find the smallest positive integer $m$ for which it is possible to choose points $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_m$ in the interior of this polygon, then draw some pairwise non-intersecting segments with endpoints in the set
$$\{A_1, A_2, \dots, A_{2n}\} \cup \{B_1, B_2, \dots, B_m\},$$
and color each of these segments with one of the given $n$ colors, so that the original polygon is thereby divided into convex quadrilaterals with the property that in each of them opposite sides have the same color.
rs.2026.1.3.rationale: Minimum interior vertices of a coloured convex quadrilateral dissection.

rs.2026.2.4.reviewed_statement: In the plane $n = 2k+1$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, points are given, no three of which are collinear. Maja and Kosta play the following game: first, Maja joins every two of these $n$ points by a segment and directs each of the segments towards one of its two endpoints, in any way she wishes. After that, the two of them play a game consisting of $k$ consecutive rounds. In each round Kosta first chooses one of the points that nobody has chosen earlier in the game, after which Maja does the same, and then the round is lost by the player towards whose point the segment between the two points chosen in that round is directed. Maja's goal is to direct the segments at the start so that, if she plays optimally afterwards, regardless of how Kosta chooses points, he cannot win any of the $k$ rounds of the game. In how many different ways can Maja achieve her goal?
rs.2026.2.4.rationale: Counting tournament orientations admitting a defensive pairing strategy.

rs.2026.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Find all functions $f : (0, +\infty) \to (0, +\infty)$ such that
$$f\left(\frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{x}\right) = \frac{f(x)}{f(y)} + \frac{f(y)}{f(x)}$$
for all $x, y \in (0, +\infty)$.

rs.2026.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $k$ and $l$ be nonnegative integers and let $r$ and $s$ be positive integers. Denote by $S$ the set of all pairs of positive integers $(a, b)$ for which
$$a \mid b^2 + kb + 1, \qquad b \mid a^2 + al + 1.$$
Prove that the pair $(r, s)$ belongs to the set $S$ if and only if the set
$$G = \{\gcd(a - r, b - s) \mid (a, b) \in S\}$$
is infinite.

rst.2004.1.1.reviewed_statement: A square $ABCD$ and a circle $\gamma$ with diameter $AB$ are given. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on the side $CD$, let $M$ and $N$ be the intersections, different from $A$ and $B$, of the segments $AP$ and $BP$ with $\gamma$, respectively, and let $Q$ be the intersection point of the lines $DM$ and $CN$. Prove that $Q \in \gamma$ and that $AQ : QB = DP : PC$.

rst.2004.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Let $a, b, c$ be real numbers such that $abc = 1$. Prove that at most two of the numbers
$$2a - \frac{1}{b}, \quad 2b - \frac{1}{c}, \quad 2c - \frac{1}{a}$$
are greater than $1$.

rst.2004.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with roots $i-1, i-2, \dots, i-n$, and let $R(x)$ and $S(x)$ be polynomials with real coefficients such that
$$P(x) = R(x) + iS(x).$$
Prove that the polynomial $R$ has $n$ real zeros. ($i$ is the imaginary unit.)

rst.2005.1.1.reviewed_statement: The sequence $x_1 = 1$, $x_2 = 4$ and $x_{n+2} = 4x_{n+1} - x_n$ for $n \ge 1$ is given. Find all positive integers $m$ such that the number $3x_n^2 + m$ is a perfect square for all positive integers $n$.
rst.2005.1.1.rationale: Integer linear recurrence and uniform square shifts.

rst.2005.1.2.reviewed_statement: How many $100$-digit positive integers are there whose decimal representation contains only odd digits and in which every two adjacent digits differ by $2$?
rst.2005.1.2.rationale: Counting odd-digit strings with prescribed adjacent differences.

rst.2005.1.3.reviewed_statement:
(a) Prove that there exists a positive integer which is divisible by $2005$ and whose sum of digits equals $2$.

(b) Let $x_n$ be the positive integer obtained by writing the positive integers from $1$ to $n$ one after another (for example, $x_1 = 1$, $x_2 = 12$, $x_3 = 123$, $\dots$, $x_{13} = 12345678910111213$). Prove that the sequence $x_1, x_2, \dots$ contains infinitely many terms divisible by $2005$.

rst.2006.1.1.rationale: Partition of an integer interval with mixed sum and product rules.

rst.2006.1.2.reviewed_statement: In the interior of a right triangle $ABC$ ($\angle ACB = 90^\circ$) a point $P$ is chosen such that $AP = 4$, $BP = 2$ and $CP = 1$. The point $Q$, the reflection of $P$ in $AC$, lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Determine the angles of triangle $ABC$.

rst.2006.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Find all positive integers $n$ and $k$, $k > 1$, such that $k$ divides each of the numbers
$$\binom{n}{1}, \binom{n}{2}, \dots, \binom{n}{n-1}.$$
rst.2006.1.3.rationale: Common divisors of all internal binomial coefficients.

rst.2016.1.1.reviewed_statement:
A sequence of polynomials $P_n(x)$ is defined by
$$P_0(x) = x^3 - 4x \quad \text{and} \quad P_{n+1}(x) = P_n(1+x)P_n(1-x) - 1.$$
Prove that the polynomial $P_{2016}(x)$ is divisible by $x^{2016}$.
rst.2016.1.1.rationale: Polynomial recurrence and order of vanishing.

rst.2016.1.2.reviewed_statement: A square $ABCD$ with side $4$ is given. Find the largest positive integer $k$ such that, for any arrangement of $k$ points strictly inside the square $ABCD$, there always exists a square of side $1$ contained in the square $ABCD$ (whose sides need not be parallel to the sides of $ABCD$) whose strict interior contains none of the $k$ points.
rst.2016.1.2.rationale: Guaranteed empty unit square among points in a larger square.

rst.2016.1.3.reviewed_statement: Denote by $w(x)$ the largest odd divisor of a positive integer $x$. If $a$ and $b$ are coprime positive integers such that $a + w(b+1)$ and $b + w(a+1)$ are powers of two, prove that $a+1$ and $b+1$ are also powers of two.

rst.2017.1.1.reviewed_statement:
A triangle $ABC$ is given. The point $D$ is the midpoint of side $BC$, and on the sides $AC$ and $AB$ the points $E$ and $F$, respectively, are chosen such that $DE = DF$ and $\angle EDF = \angle BAC$. Prove that
$$DE \ge \frac{AB + AC}{4}.$$

rst.2017.1.2.reviewed_statement: A step is the function which maps an ordered pair of positive integers $(x, y)$ with exactly one even coordinate to the pair $\left(\frac{x}{2}, y + \frac{x}{2}\right)$ if $2 \mid x$, and to the pair $\left(x + \frac{y}{2}, \frac{y}{2}\right)$ if $2 \mid y$. Prove that for every odd positive integer $n$, $n > 1$, there exists an even positive integer $b$, $b < n$, such that by successively applying finitely many steps to the ordered pair $(n, b)$ one obtains the ordered pair $(b, n)$.
rst.2017.1.2.rationale: Parity-controlled redistribution of two integer coordinates.

rst.2017.1.3.reviewed_statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is called lively if for all $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$
$$f(a + b - 1) = \underbrace{f(f(\cdots f}_{a \text{ times}}(b)\cdots)).$$
Let $g$ be a lively function such that $g(A + 2018) = g(A) + 1$ for some $A \ge 2$.

a) Prove that $g(n + 2017^{2017}) = g(n)$ for all $n \ge A + 2$.

b) If $g(A + 2017^{2017}) \neq g(A)$, determine $g(n)$ for $n \le A - 1$.
rst.2017.1.3.rationale: Natural-number iteration identity and eventual periodicity.

rst.2017.2.4.reviewed_statement: An $n \times n$ square is divided into unit squares. One has to place on it a certain number of isosceles right triangles with hypotenuse $2$, with vertices at vertices of the unit squares, in such a way that every side of every unit square belongs to exactly one triangle (i.e. lies in its interior or on its boundary). Determine all values of $n$ for which this is possible.
rst.2017.2.4.rationale: Lattice triangle placement covering each grid edge exactly once.

rst.2017.2.5.rationale: Sharp cyclic sequence parameter and an even-length criterion.
