itt.2010.1.1.reviewed_statement:
There are $n$ cards, where $n\ge50$ is an integer. Each card has one black side and one blue side. Initially the cards lie in a row on a table, all showing their blue sides. Alberto and Barbara, standing on the same side of the table, take turns choosing a block of $50$ consecutive cards whose leftmost card is blue, and turning over all the cards in that block. Alberto starts. The game ends when no legal move is possible; the player making the last legal move wins.

(a) Prove that the game terminates for every $n$.

(b) Determine, in terms of $n$, which player has a winning strategy.

itt.2010.1.2.reviewed_statement: A cyclic quadrilateral has the property that the midpoints of its sides also form a cyclic quadrilateral. Prove that the area of the disk bounded by the circumcircle of the smaller quadrilateral is at most half the area of the disk bounded by the circumcircle of the larger quadrilateral.

itt.2010.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers such that $$\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c=a+b+c.$$ Prove that $$\frac1{(2a+b+c)^2}+\frac1{(2b+c+a)^2}+\frac1{(2c+a+b)^2}\le\frac3{16}.$$

itt.2010.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all solutions $(p,n;x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_p)$ of $$\sum_{i=0}^{p}x_i^{p!}=p^n,$$ where $p$ is prime, $n$ is a nonnegative integer, and $x_0\le x_1\le\cdots\le x_p$ are nonnegative integers.

itt.2010.2.5.reviewed_statement: A football tournament has $n\ge3$ teams. Each team plays each other team exactly once. A win earns $3$ points, a loss $0$ points, and a draw $1$ point for each team. At the end, all teams have distinct point totals forming an arithmetic progression, and the last-place team has exactly one point. Determine all possible configurations: the value of $n$, the final standings, and the results of every match.

itt.2010.2.6.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, an excircle touches side $BC$ at $D$ and the extensions of $AB$ and $AC$ at $E$ and $F$, respectively. Let $P$ be the perpendicular projection of $D$ onto $EF$, let $M$ be the midpoint of $EF$, and let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of $ABC$. Prove that $P$ lies on $\Gamma$ if and only if $M$ lies on $\Gamma$.

itt.2011.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. The line parallel to $BC$ and tangent to the incircle meets $AB$ at $A_1$ and $AC$ at $A_2$. Define $B_1,B_2,C_1,C_2$ analogously. Prove that $$AA_1\cdot AA_2+BB_1\cdot BB_2+CC_1\cdot CC_2\ge\frac19(AB^2+BC^2+CA^2),$$ and determine the equality cases.

itt.2011.1.2.reviewed_statement: At a concert, $k$ singers are to perform one after another. Each singer specifies a possibly empty set of other singers and asks to perform after every singer in that set. Determine whether there can be exactly $2010$ performance orders satisfying all the requests in each of the following cases: (a) $k=80$; (b) $k=70$; (c) $k=20$.

itt.2011.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest positive integer $n$ for which there exist polynomials $p_1(x),\ldots,p_n(x)$ with rational coefficients such that $$x^2+7=[p_1(x)]^2+\cdots+[p_n(x)]^2.$$
itt.2011.1.3.rationale: A polynomial sum-of-squares identity over rational coefficients combines polynomial structure with rational arithmetic.

itt.2011.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $n>1$ be odd. Let $S$ be the set of integers $k$ with $1\le k\le n$ that are relatively prime to $n$, and let $T$ be the set of $k\in S$ for which $k+1$ is relatively prime to $n$. For each $k\in S$, let $r_k$ be the remainder on division by $n$ of $$\frac{k^{|S|}-1}{n}.$$ Prove that $$\prod_{k\in T}(r_k-r_{n-k})\equiv |S|^{|T|}\pmod n.$$

itt.2011.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral such that the lines $BC$ and $AD$ meet at $P$. Let $Q\ne B$ lie on line $BP$ and satisfy $PQ=BP$. Construct parallelograms $CAQR$ and $DBCS$. Prove that $C,Q,R,S$ lie on a circle.

itt.2011.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_{100}$ be nonnegative real numbers satisfying $x_i+x_{i+1}+x_{i+2}\le1$ for every $i=1,\ldots,100$, with indices taken modulo $100$ so that $x_{101}=x_1$ and $x_{102}=x_2$. Find the maximum possible value of $$S=\sum_{i=1}^{100}x_ix_{i+2}.$$

itt.2012.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine whether there exists a sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of positive integers satisfying both of the following conditions: $$a_{n+1}=a_n+\tau(n)\quad\text{for every }n\ge1,$$ where $\tau(n)$ is the number of positive divisors of $n$; and at least two consecutive terms of the sequence are perfect squares.

itt.2012.1.2.reviewed_statement: A convex $n$-gon is triangulated by diagonals that do not intersect inside the polygon. Each triangle is coloured white or black, with triangles sharing a side always having different colours. Determine, in terms of $n$, the greatest possible difference between the number of white triangles and the number of black triangles.
itt.2012.1.2.rationale: A polygon triangulation and its adjacency colouring are both essential to the extremal count.

itt.2012.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcentre $O$ and circumcircle $\Gamma$. Let $D$ lie on segment $BC$, distinct from its endpoints and midpoint. The circumcircle of $BOD$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $K$ and line $AB$ again at $E$. The circumcircle of $COD$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $L$ and line $AC$ again at $F$. The circumcircle of $AEF$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $M$. Suppose that $E$ lies inside segment $AB$ and $F$ inside segment $AC$. Prove that triangles $ABC$ and $MKL$ are congruent.

itt.2012.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $\ell$ pass through its circumcentre parallel to the bisector of angle $A$. Prove that $\ell$ passes through the orthocentre of $ABC$ if and only if $AB=AC$ or $\angle BAC=120^\circ$.

itt.2012.2.5.reviewed_statement: Consider $$P(x)=(x+d_1)(x+d_2)\cdots(x+d_9),$$ where $d_1,\ldots,d_9$ are nine distinct integers. Prove that there is an integer $N$ such that for every integer $x\ge N$, $P(x)$ is divisible by a prime greater than $20$.

itt.2012.2.6.reviewed_statement:
For a function $f$ from a set to itself and a positive integer $k$, write $f^{(k)}$ for its $k$th iterate, defined by $f^{(1)}(x)=f(x)$ and $f^{(k+1)}(x)=f(f^{(k)}(x))$.

(a) Find all functions $f$ from the positive integers to the positive integers such that $$f^{(n+1)}(n)<f(n+1)$$ for every positive integer $n$.

(b) Find all pairs $(f,g)$ of functions from the positive integers to the positive integers such that $$f^{(g(n)+1)}(n)+g^{(f(n))}(n)=f(n+1)-g(n+1)+1$$ for every positive integer $n$.
itt.2012.2.6.rationale: Functional iteration is constrained by integer-valued domains and integer inequalities.

itt.2013.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n>m>0$ be integers. Determine, in terms of $n$ and $m$, the greatest possible value of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_m^2$ among all $n$-tuples of real numbers $0\le x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$ satisfying $x_1+\cdots+x_n=1$.

itt.2013.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB\ne AC$ and circumcentre $O$. Let the angle bisector from $A$ meet $BC$ at $D$, and let $E$ be the reflection of $D$ in the midpoint of $BC$. The perpendicular to $BC$ through $D$ meets line $AO$ at $X$, and the perpendicular to $BC$ through $E$ meets line $AD$ at $Y$. Prove that $BXCY$ is cyclic.

itt.2013.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be nonzero polynomials with integer coefficients and $\deg f>\deg g$.

(a) Suppose that $pf(x)+g(x)$ has an integer root for infinitely many primes $p$. Prove that $f(x)$ has an integer root.

(b) Suppose that $pf(x)+g(x)$ has a rational root for infinitely many primes $p$. Prove that $f(x)$ has a rational root.
itt.2013.1.3.rationale: Polynomial roots over integers and rationals are controlled by varying prime coefficients.

itt.2013.2.4.reviewed_statement: Call a set $A$ of integers plump if, for every $x,y\in A$, possibly equal, and every integer $k$, we have $x^2+kxy+y^2\in A$. Find all pairs of integers $(m,n)$ for which the only plump set containing both $m$ and $n$ is $\mathbb Z$.

itt.2013.2.5.reviewed_statement:
For every positive integer $n$, let $C(n)$ be the largest integer $k$ for which there are $k$ disjoint pairs of elements of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ whose pair sums are $k$ distinct integers at most $n$. Each pair contains two distinct elements, and no element belongs to more than one pair.

(a) Determine $C(12)$ and $C(13)$.

(b) Determine $C(n)$ for every positive integer $n$.
itt.2013.2.5.rationale: Disjoint pair packing must satisfy distinct bounded integer sums.

itt.2013.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral. Circle $\Gamma_1$ passes through $A,B$ and is tangent to side $CD$ at $E$. Circle $\Gamma_2$ passes through $B,C$ and is tangent to side $DA$ at $F$. Circle $\Gamma_3$ passes through $C,D$ and is tangent to side $AB$ at $G$. Circle $\Gamma_4$ passes through $D,A$ and is tangent to side $BC$ at $H$. Prove that $EG$ and $FH$ are perpendicular.

itt.2014.1.1.reviewed_statement: Define a sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ by $a_1=a_2=1$ and, for every $n\ge1$, $$a_{2n+1}=2a_{2n}-a_n,\qquad a_{2n+2}=2a_{2n+1}.$$ Prove that $a_n$ is divisible by $5$ whenever $n>3$ and $n-3$ is divisible by $8$.

itt.2014.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be prime, and let $(x_1,\ldots,x_p)$ be a $p$-tuple of integers such that $$x_1^n+\cdots+x_p^n\equiv0\pmod p$$ for every positive integer $n$. Prove that $x_1\equiv\cdots\equiv x_p\pmod p$.

itt.2014.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $\omega_1$ be a circle with centre $O$, let $AB$ be a diameter, and let $C\in\omega_1$ satisfy $90^\circ<\angle AOC<180^\circ$. Let $K$ lie on line $OC$ with $C$ between $K$ and $O$, and let $\omega_2$ have centre $K$ and pass through $C$. Let $E$ be the other intersection of line $KB$ with $\omega_1$, and let $S,T\in\omega_2$ be the points for which $ES$ and $ET$ are tangent to $\omega_2$. Prove that lines $AC,EK,ST$ are concurrent.

itt.2014.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $A_0B_0C_0$ be a triangle of area $\sqrt2$ in the Cartesian plane. Let the vertices of $A_1B_1C_1$ be the excentres of $A_0B_0C_0$, let the vertices of $A_2B_2C_2$ be the excentres of $A_1B_1C_1$, and continue in this way. Determine whether this procedure can eventually produce a triangle whose vertices all have both coordinates rational.
itt.2014.2.4.rationale: Iterated geometric excentre constructions are tested against rational-coordinate arithmetic.

itt.2014.2.5.reviewed_statement: A mathematics competition has $30$ contestants and $8$ problems. Each problem is either solved or not solved. After the competition, the value of each problem is set equal to the number of contestants who did not solve it: for example, a problem solved by everyone is worth $0$ points, and one solved by $8$ contestants is worth $22$ points. Each contestant receives the sum of the values of the problems they solved. There is a unique last-place contestant, whose score is strictly below everyone else's. Find the largest possible score of this contestant.

itt.2014.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c,p,q,r$ be positive integers satisfying $$a^p+b^q+c^r=a^q+b^r+c^p=a^r+b^p+c^q.$$ Prove that $a=b=c$ or $p=q=r$.
itt.2014.2.6.rationale: An equality of integer powers combines exponential algebra with discrete integer parameters.

itt.2015.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine whether there exists a function $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ such that $$(x^2+y)f(yf(x)+f(y^2))=x^3f(y^2f(x))$$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

itt.2015.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. Lines $AD$ and $BC$ meet at $E$, and diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meet at $P$. The circumcircles of $APD$ and $BPC$ meet again at $Q$. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $AD,BC$, respectively, and let $K=AC\cap MN$ and $L=BD\cap MN$.

(a) Prove that $EMQN$ is cyclic.

(b) Prove that the circumcircles of $AMK$ and $BNL$ pass through $Q$.

(c) Prove that these two circles pass through a common point on line $AB$.

itt.2015.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge2$ be an integer, and let $$A_n=\{2^n-2^k:k\in\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}\}.$$ Determine, in terms of $n$, the largest positive integer that cannot be written as a sum of one or more, not necessarily distinct, elements of $A_n$.

itt.2015.2.4.reviewed_statement: A country has $20$ cities and $18$ aeroplanes. Each aeroplane regularly follows a directed circular route of five legs visiting five distinct cities. Each city is visited by the routes of at least three aeroplanes. For each pair of cities, at most one aeroplane connects them directly, in either direction, without an intermediate stop. Prove that every city can be reached from every other city by using these flights appropriately.

itt.2015.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs of positive integers $(x,y)$ with the following property: whenever $a,b$ are relatively prime positive divisors of $x^3+y^3$, the number $a+b-1$ is also a divisor of $x^3+y^3$.

itt.2015.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB>BC$, circumcentre $O$, and circumcircle $\Omega$. Let $M$ be the second intersection of the angle bisector from $B$ with $\Omega$, let $K$ be the midpoint of $BM$, and let $\Gamma$ be the circle with diameter $BM$. The bisector rays of $\angle AOB$ and $\angle BOC$ meet $\Gamma$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively.

(a) Prove that $PQKO$ is cyclic.

(b) Let $R$ be the point on line $PQ$ satisfying $RB=RM$. Prove that $BR$ and $AC$ are parallel.

itt.2016.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with an interior point $P$ such that $\angle APD=\angle BPC=90^\circ$ and $PA\cdot PD=PB\cdot PC$. Let $O$ be the circumcentre of $CPD$. Prove that line $OP$ passes through the midpoint of $AB$.

itt.2016.1.2.reviewed_statement: On a certain day, $2016$ customers visited a shopping centre. Each entered once, stayed for some time, and then left without returning. A group is called simultaneous if all its members were inside the shopping centre together at some instant. A group is called sequential if no two of its members were inside together, even for an instant. Find the largest integer $k$ such that, regardless of the arrival and departure times, there must be a simultaneous group of at least $k$ customers or a sequential group of at least $k$ customers.

itt.2016.1.3.reviewed_statement: Prove that there is no function $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ such that $$f(f(x)+y)=f(x)+3x+yf(y)$$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

itt.2016.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b$ be positive integers such that $a!+b!$ divides $a!\cdot b!$. Prove that $3a\ge2b+2$.

itt.2016.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $(a_n)$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $$a_{n+1}\ge\frac{na_n}{a_n^2+(n-1)}$$ for every positive integer $n$. Prove that $a_1+\cdots+a_n\ge n$ for every $n\ge2$.

itt.2016.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB\ne AC$, and let $D,E,F$ be the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Let $\omega$ pass through $A$ and be tangent to line $BC$ at $D$. Circle $\omega$ meets line $AB$ again at $X$, line $AC$ again at $Y$, line $DE$ again at $R$, and line $DF$ again at $S$. Let $X\prime$ be the reflection of $X$ in $F$, and $Y\prime$ the reflection of $Y$ in $E$. Line $X\prime Y\prime$ meets line $AD$ at $Q$ and line $EF$ at $M$. Finally, let $P$ be the other intersection of $\omega$ with line $AM$.

(a) Prove that $R,S$ lie on line $X\prime Y\prime$.

(b) Prove that $Q$ lies on the radical axis of the circumcircles of $DCR$ and $DBS$.

(c) Prove that $AQ=QP$.

itt.2017.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $$f(a^2)-f(b^2)\le(f(a)+b)(a-f(b))$$ for all real numbers $a,b$.

itt.2017.1.2.reviewed_statement:
(a) Find all triples $(a,b,n)$ of positive integers with $n\ge2$ such that $n^{a+b}-1$ is a multiple of $n^a+n^b+1$.

(b) Find all triples $(a,b,n)$ of positive integers with $n\ge2$ such that $n^{a+b}-1$ is a multiple of $n^a+5n^b+1$.

itt.2017.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC\ne BC$ and incentre $I$. Line $BI$ meets $AC$ at $D$. The line through $D$ perpendicular to $AC$ meets $AI$ at $E$. Let $J$ be the reflection of $I$ across line $AC$. Prove that the circumcircle of $BED$ passes through $J$.

itt.2017.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}$ such that $$xf(x)+[f(y)]^2+2xf(y)$$ is a perfect square for all positive integers $x,y$.
itt.2017.2.4.rationale: An integer-valued functional condition requires every expression to be a perfect square.

itt.2017.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge5$ be an integer relatively prime to $6$. The vertices of a regular $n$-gon are coloured with three colours, with an odd number of vertices of each colour. Prove that there is an isosceles triangle whose vertices have three different colours.
itt.2017.2.5.rationale: Colouring parity and a regular-polygon isosceles-triangle condition are both essential.

itt.2017.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all positive real numbers $\alpha$ for which there exists a strictly increasing sequence $(x_n)$ of positive integers such that $$x_{2n}+x_{2n-1}=\alpha x_n$$ for every positive integer $n$.
itt.2017.2.6.rationale: A real parameter in a sequence equation is constrained by strictly increasing integer terms.

itt.2018.1.1.reviewed_statement: A rectangle $R$ has side lengths that are odd positive integers. It is partitioned into smaller rectangles, all with integer side lengths. Prove that at least one smaller rectangle has the property that the distances of its sides from the corresponding sides of $R$ are either all even or all odd.
itt.2018.1.1.rationale: A rectangle partition is combined with parity conditions on geometric distances.

itt.2018.1.2.reviewed_statement: A sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of real numbers satisfies $$a_n=-\max\{a_i+a_j:i+j=n\}$$ for every $n\ge2018$, where $i,j$ are positive integers. Prove that the sequence is bounded: there is a real number $M$ such that $|a_n|\le M$ for every positive integer $n$.

itt.2018.1.3.reviewed_statement: Call a rational number terminating if its decimal expansion has only finitely many nonzero digits. For every positive integer $m$, let $S(m)$ be the set of positive integers $k$ for which there exists $c\in\{1,2,\ldots,2018\}$ such that $$k=\min\left\{i\ge1:\frac{10^i-1}{cm}\text{ is a terminating rational number}\right\}.$$ Find the largest possible number of elements of $S(m)$ as $m$ ranges over the positive integers.

itt.2018.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be prime. Alberto and Barbara take turns forming a decimal number with $p$ digit positions, allowing leading zeroes. On each turn, the player chooses a position not previously chosen by either player and places a digit from $0$ to $9$ in it. Alberto moves first. Alberto wins if the final number is divisible by $p$; otherwise Barbara wins. Prove that Alberto has a winning strategy.
itt.2018.2.4.rationale: A turn-based digit-placement game has an arithmetic divisibility winning condition.

itt.2018.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. The $A$-excircle $\omega$ touches side $BC$ at $D$, line $AC$ at $E$, and line $AB$ at $F$. The circumcircle of $AEF$ meets line $BC$ at $P,Q$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AD$. Prove that the circumcircle of $MPQ$ is tangent to $\omega$.

itt.2018.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $S$ be a finite set, let $F$ be the set of all functions from $S$ to $S$, and let $f\in F$. Write $T=f(S)=\{f(x):x\in S\}$. Suppose that for every $g\in F$ with $g\ne f$, there exists $s\in S$ such that $$f(g(f(s)))\ne g(f(g(s))).$$ Prove that for every $t\in T$ there exists $x\in T$ such that $f(x)=t$.
itt.2018.2.6.rationale: Composition identities for self-maps on a finite set lead to an image-surjectivity conclusion.

itt.2019.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$. The circle with centre $A$ passing through $D$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $X,Y$, where $X$ lies on the same side of line $AD$ as $B$. Prove that $\angle BXD=\angle CYD$.

itt.2019.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a_0,a_1,\ldots$ be a sequence of positive integers such that, for every $n\ge1$, $a_n$ is the smallest positive integer for which $a_0+a_1+\cdots+a_n$ is divisible by $n$. Prove that there exists a positive integer $m$ such that $a_n=a_m$ for every $n\ge m$.

itt.2019.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Define $(a_n)_{n\ge0}$ by $$a_n=2^n+2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.$$ (a) Prove that infinitely many terms of this sequence can be written as a sum of two or more distinct terms of the same sequence.

(b) Prove that infinitely many terms of the sequence cannot be written as a sum of two or more distinct terms of the same sequence.
itt.2019.1.3.rationale: An explicit integer sequence is studied through distinct-term additive representations.

itt.2019.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$ for which there exists a positive integer $n$ such that $na$ and $nb$ have the same number of positive divisors.

itt.2019.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $P$ be a point such that line $PA$ is parallel to line $BC$ and $PB<PC$. Let $X$ lie on line $PB$ and $Y$ on line $PC$ such that $B$ lies on segment $PX$, $C$ lies on segment $PY$, and $\angle PXM=\angle PYM$. Prove that $APXY$ is cyclic.

itt.2019.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find the largest integer $k$ with the following property: whenever a $5\times5$ array is filled with the integers $1,2,\ldots,25$, each used exactly once, there is a $2\times2$ square of adjacent cells whose entries have sum at least $k$.

th.2021.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB=AC$. Let $\omega$ be a circle centred at $A$ with radius strictly less than $AB$. Draw tangents from $B$ and $C$ to $\omega$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Suppose that line $PQ$ meets line $BC$ at $M$. Prove that $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$.

th.2021.1.2.reviewed_statement: Determine all sequences $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ of positive integers satisfying $$(n^2+1)a_{n+1}-a_n=n^3+n^2+1$$ for every positive integer $n$.

th.2021.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers satisfying $ab+bc+ca=abc$. Determine the minimum value of $$a^a bc+b^b ca+c^c ab.$$

th.2021.1.4.reviewed_statement: Kan Krao Park is a circular park with $21$ entrances and a straight walkway joining every pair of entrances. No three walkways meet at a single point. Some walkways are paved with bricks and the others with asphalt. At each intersection of two walkways, excluding the entrances, a lotus is planted if the walkways have the same paving material, and a waterlily if they have different paving materials. A walkway is decorated with lights if and only if the same type of plant occurs at at least $45$ distinct points along it. Prove that at least $11$ walkways are decorated with lights and have the same paving material.
th.2021.1.4.rationale: The chord intersection geometry determines a two-colour combinatorial threshold.

th.2021.1.5.reviewed_statement: Determine all triples $(p,m,k)$ of positive integers such that $p$ is prime, $m$ and $k$ are odd, and $$m^4+4^kp^4\mid m^2(m^4-4^kp^4).$$

th.2021.2.6.reviewed_statement: The cheering team of Ubon Ratchathani University sits in an amphitheatre with $441$ seats arranged in a $21\times21$ grid. Each seat is occupied by exactly one person, and each person has a blue sign and a yellow sign. Count the ways for each person to raise one sign so that every row and every column has an odd number of people raising blue signs.

th.2021.2.7.reviewed_statement: Determine all functions $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $$f(xy)=f(x)f(y)f(x+y)$$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

th.2021.2.8.reviewed_statement: Let $P$ lie inside an acute triangle $ABC$. Lines $BP$ and $CP$ meet sides $AC$ and $AB$ at $D$ and $E$, respectively. The circles with diameters $BD$ and $CE$ meet at $S,T$. Prove that if $A,S,T$ are collinear, then $P$ lies on a median of $ABC$.

th.2021.2.9.reviewed_statement: Let $S$ be a set of positive integers such that whenever $a,b\in S$ and $a<b$, the integer $b-a$ divides $\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$ and the quotient belongs to $S$. Prove that $|S|\le2$.

th.2021.2.10.reviewed_statement: Let $d\ge13$ be an integer and let $$P(x)=a_dx^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+a_1x+a_0$$ be a polynomial of degree $d$ with complex coefficients such that $a_n=a_{d-n}$ for all $n\in\{0,1,\ldots,d\}$. Prove that if $P$ has no double roots, it has two distinct roots $z_1,z_2$ with $|z_1-z_2|<1$.
th.2021.2.10.rationale: Symmetric complex-polynomial coefficients constrain distances between roots in the complex plane.

th.2023.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $A$ be a set of $20$ consecutive positive integers such that neither their sum nor their product is divisible by $23$. Prove that their product is not a perfect square.

th.2023.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle ABC=90^\circ$. Let $D$ lie on segment $AB$, with $D\ne A,B$, and let $E$ lie on line $AB$ such that $B$ is the midpoint of $DE$. Let $I$ be the incentre of $ACE$ and $J$ the $A$-excentre of $ACD$. Prove that the perpendicular bisector of $BC$ bisects segment $IJ$.

th.2023.1.3.reviewed_statement: Determine all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $$f(x)f(y)f(x-y)=x^2f(y)-y^2f(x)$$ for all real numbers $x,y$.

th.2023.1.4.reviewed_statement: A table-tennis tournament has $101$ contestants, and every pair plays exactly once. In each match the first player to score $11$ points wins. At the end of the tournament there are matches with scores $11$–$0$ and $11$–$10$. Prove that there are three contestants $A,B,C$ such that the losers score equally many points in matches $AB$ and $AC$, but a different number of points in match $BC$.

th.2023.1.5.reviewed_statement: Let $\ell$ be a line in the plane and let $90^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$. Consider distinct points $P,Q,R$ satisfying: (i) $P\in\ell$ and $PQ\perp\ell$; (ii) $R$ lies on the same side of $\ell$ as $Q$ and $R\notin\ell$; (iii) for every pair of points $A,B\in\ell$, if $\angle ARB=\theta$, then $\angle AQB\ge\theta$. Find the minimum value of $\angle PQR$.

th.2023.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c,x,y$ be positive real numbers with $abc=1$. Prove that $$\frac{a^5}{xc+yb}+\frac{b^5}{xa+yc}+\frac{c^5}{xb+ya}\ge\frac9{(x+y)(a^2+b^2+c^2)}.$$

th.2023.2.7.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $S=\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$, and define the set of points $$A=\{(x,y)\in S\times S:-1\le x-y\le1\}.$$ Lamps are placed at points of $A$, each illuminating all points within distance $1.01$. Determine the minimum number of lamps needed to illuminate every point of $A$.
th.2023.2.7.rationale: A geometric distance condition on a finite lattice determines a minimum covering count.

th.2023.2.8.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. The tangents to its circumcircle at $A,B$ meet at $T$, and line $CT$ meets side $AB$ at $D$. Let $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ be the circumcircles of $CAD,CBD$, respectively. Line $TA$ meets $\Gamma_1$ again at $E$, and line $TB$ meets $\Gamma_2$ again at $F$. Line $EF$ meets sides $AC,BC$ at $P,Q$, respectively. Prove that $EF=PQ+AB$.

th.2023.2.9.reviewed_statement: Prove that there is an infinite sequence of positive integers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ such that for every positive integer $k$, the number $a_k^2+a_k+2023$ has at least $k$ distinct positive divisors.

th.2023.2.10.reviewed_statement: To celebrate the $20$th Thailand Mathematical Olympiad, Ratchasima Witthayalai School placed flags around the Thao Suranari Monument. Each flag has exactly one colour, and at least two colours are used. The number of flags is odd. The flags occupy the vertices of a regular polygon, one flag at each vertex, and the flags of each individual colour also occupy the vertices of a regular polygon. Prove that at least three colours occur on equally many flags.
th.2023.2.10.rationale: Colour-class counts are constrained by regular-polygon geometry and odd parity.

uy.2011.0.1.reviewed_statement: Let $AB$ be an arc of a circle $\Gamma$, and let $P$ vary on that arc. Let $D$ be the midpoint of arc $AP$ not containing $B$, and $E$ the midpoint of arc $BP$ not containing $A$. Let $\Gamma_1$ be the circle with centre $D$ passing through $A$, and $\Gamma_2$ the circle with centre $E$ passing through $B$. Prove that the line through the intersection points of $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ passes through a fixed point.

uy.2011.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $O$ be a point and $A$ a set of $15$ points in the same plane as $O$. Each point of $A$ is at distance less than $1$ from $O$, and no two points of $A$ are collinear with $O$. Prove that there is a triangle with one vertex at $O$ and its other two vertices in $A$ whose area is less than $\frac14$.
uy.2011.0.2.rationale: A finite planar-point configuration forces a triangle-area bound.

uy.2011.0.3.reviewed_statement: Find all natural numbers $n$ such that $2^{2n}+2^n+1$ is divisible by $21$.

uy.2011.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z_{>0}$ satisfy $$f(x+y)f(x-y)=[f(x)f(y)]^2$$ for all integers $x,y$, with $f(1)\ne1$. Prove that $\log_{f(1)}f(z)$ is a perfect square for every integer $z$.
uy.2011.0.4.rationale: A functional equation has a positive-integer codomain and a perfect-square logarithm conclusion.

uy.2012.0.1.reviewed_statement: There are $n$ lines in a plane, no two parallel and no three concurrent. Into how many regions do these lines divide the plane?
uy.2012.0.1.rationale: The regions formed by a geometric line arrangement require a combinatorial count.

uy.2012.0.2.reviewed_statement: In a country, coins have denominations $2^k$ and $3^k$ units, where $k$ may be any positive integer. Prove that any price can be paid, either exactly or by receiving an exact amount of change.

uy.2012.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle, and let $M,N,P$ be the midpoints of $AB,BC,AC$, respectively. Let the altitude from $A$ meet line $BC$ at $H$. The perpendiculars from $H$ to lines $MN,NP,PM$ meet those lines at $K,J,L$, respectively. Prove that $K,J,L$ are collinear.

uy.2012.0.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that for positive real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ and positive integers $k,n$, $$x_1x_2\cdots x_k\bigl(x_1^{n-1}+x_2^{n-1}+\cdots+x_k^{n-1}\bigr)\le x_1^{n+k-1}+x_2^{n+k-1}+\cdots+x_k^{n+k-1}.$$

uy.2013.0.1.reviewed_statement: Find all primes $p$ for which $p^2+11$ has exactly six distinct positive divisors, including $1$ and the number itself.

uy.2013.0.2.reviewed_statement: A box contains $2013$ green balls, $2013$ yellow balls, $2013$ red balls and $2013$ blue balls. Outside the box there are enough balls of each colour to carry out all the operations below. The allowed operations are: (i) remove four balls of the same colour without replacing them; (ii) remove one green, one yellow and one red ball, and replace them with one blue ball; (iii) remove three blue balls and replace them with one yellow ball; (iv) remove two red balls and replace them with one green ball; (v) remove two yellow balls and replace them with one red ball. Prove that if exactly one ball remains in the box after finitely many allowed operations, it must be red.

uy.2013.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $m$ be a positive even integer. Prove that if $$x=m+\frac1{m+\frac1{m+\frac1{\ddots}}},$$ then $x$ has the form $n+\sqrt{n^2+1}$ for a positive integer $n$.

uy.2013.0.4.reviewed_statement: Two circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ meet at $A,B$. The common tangent nearer to $A$ touches $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ at $C,D$, respectively. The line through $A$ parallel to $CD$ meets $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ again at $E,F$, respectively. Line $DA$ meets $\Gamma_1$ again at $G\ne A$ and meets line $BC$ at $I$. Similarly, line $CA$ meets $\Gamma_2$ again at $H\ne A$ and meets line $BD$ at $J$. Let $K=CG\cap BE$ and $L=DH\cap BF$. Prove that: (a) $KI\parallel CD$ and $JL\parallel CD$; (b) $K,I,J,L$ are collinear.

uy.2014.0.1.reviewed_statement: Primes $p,q,r$ with $p+q<111$ satisfy $$\frac{p+q}{r}=p-q+r.$$ Find the largest possible value of $pqr$.

uy.2014.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $B,C,G,H$ lie on a circle with centre $A$ and radius $R$. Point $G$ lies on the extension of the median of triangle $ABC$ from $B$, and $H$ lies on the extension of its altitude from $B$. Let $X=AC\cap GH$. Prove that $AX=2R$.

uy.2014.0.3.reviewed_statement: Six points lie inside or on the boundary of a square of side length $3$. Prove that two of the six points are at distance less than $2$.
uy.2014.0.3.rationale: A finite packing of points in a square forces a distance bound.

uy.2014.0.4.reviewed_statement: Find all polynomials $P(x)$ with real coefficients satisfying $$(x^2-6x+8)P(x)=(x^2+2x)P(x-2)$$ for every real number $x$.

uy.2015.0.1.reviewed_statement: Ana and Beto repeatedly roll a six-sided die. After each roll they write on a blackboard the average of all the rolls so far. For example, if the rolls begin $1,4,3,4,2,6,\ldots$, the board includes $$\frac{1+4}{2}=\frac52,\qquad\frac{1+4+3}{3}=\frac83,\qquad\frac{1+4+3+4}{4}=3.$$ After several hours the board is full. They erase all the numbers except the last three averages, which, in order, are $$\frac{196}{61},\qquad\frac{172}{53},\qquad\frac{211}{65}.$$ Determine how many times they rolled the die and the result of the last roll, and prove that your answer is unique.

uy.2015.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcentre $O$ and orthocentre $H$, with $\angle BAC=60^\circ$ and $AB>AC$. Let $BE,CF$ be the altitudes to $CA,AB$, respectively. Let $K$ lie on segment $BE$ with $BK=CH$. Determine $\frac{HK}{HO}$.

uy.2015.0.3.reviewed_statement: A $9\times9$ square is divided into $81$ unit square cells. Eight cells are coloured black and the others remain white. An entirely white rectangle, possibly a square, is cut out along grid lines. What is the largest area that can be guaranteed for such a rectangle, regardless of the positions of the black cells?
uy.2015.0.3.rationale: A grid colouring determines a guaranteed geometric rectangle area.

uy.2015.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z$ satisfy $f(1)=0$, $f(p)=1$ for every prime $p$, and $$f(xy)=yf(x)+xf(y)$$ for all positive integers $x,y$. Determine the smallest integer $n\ge2015$ such that $f(n)=n$.
uy.2015.0.4.rationale: An integer-valued product-rule function is constrained at prime arguments.

uy.2016.0.1.reviewed_statement: Let $P(x)=x^3+ax+b$, where $a,b$ are integers. Suppose that there are integers $y,z$ for which $P(y)-P(z)$ is divisible by $3$ but not by $9$. Prove that $a$ is not divisible by $3$.
uy.2016.0.1.rationale: Values of an integer-coefficient polynomial are constrained by divisibility.

uy.2016.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AC=AB$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be the points where its incircle touches $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Line $CZ$ meets the incircle at $Z$ and $L$, and line $YL$ meets line $BC$ at $M$. Prove that $XM=MC$.

uy.2016.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Prove that $n$ divides $\binom{n}{m}$ for every $m=1,\ldots,n-1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.

uy.2016.0.4.reviewed_statement: Consider $2016$ polynomials of degree $4$ whose roots and leading coefficients all belong to $C=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$. Find the largest number of occurrences of the same polynomial that is guaranteed.
uy.2016.0.4.rationale: Root multiplicities and leading coefficients give a finite family of polynomials to count.

uy.2017.0.2.reviewed_statement:
The figure shows Pascal's triangle through row $5$. Consider Pascal's triangle through row $2047$. Determine the number of odd entries written in the triangle.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/uy_2017_p2_fig.png
uy.2017.0.2.rationale: The parity of binomial coefficients determines a count in Pascal's triangle.

uy.2017.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $I$ be the incentre of an acute triangle $ABC$, and let $\Gamma_C$ be its excircle opposite $C$. Circle $\Gamma_C$ touches side $AB$ at $D$, and line $DI$ meets $\Gamma_C$ again at $S$. Let $P$ be the midpoint of $DI$. Prove that $PASB$ is cyclic.

uy.2017.0.4.reviewed_statement: For each natural number $n\ge2$, let $a_n$ be the largest prime not exceeding $n$, and $b_n$ the smallest prime greater than $n$. For example, $a_2=2,b_2=3$, and $a_{20}=19,b_{20}=23$. Calculate $$S=\frac1{a_2b_2}+\frac1{a_3b_3}+\frac1{a_4b_4}+\cdots+\frac1{a_{2016}b_{2016}}.$$

cl.2013.0.1.reviewed_statement: Prove that the equation $$x^x+y^y=z^z$$ has no solutions in integers.

cl.2013.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ be a natural number such that $a+n^2$ can be written as a sum of two squares for every natural number $n$. Prove that $a$ is the square of a natural number.

cl.2013.0.3.reviewed_statement: The incircle of triangle $ABC$ touches $AC$ and $BC$ at $E$ and $D$, respectively. The excircle opposite $A$ touches lines $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$ at $A_1$, $B_1$ and $C_1$, respectively. Let $L=DE\cap A_1B_1$. Prove that $L$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $A_1BC_1$.

cl.2014.0.1.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $$f(x+1)=\frac12+\sqrt{f(x)-f(x)^2}$$ for every real $x$. Prove that there is a real number $b>0$ such that $f(x+b)=f(x)$ for every real $x$.

cl.2014.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $P,Q,R$ lie on sides $AB,BC,CA$, respectively, such that $$\frac{AP}{AB}=\frac{BQ}{BC}=\frac{CR}{CA}=\frac1n,$$ where $n$ is a positive integer. Segments $AQ$ and $CP$ meet at $D$, segments $BR$ and $AQ$ meet at $E$, and segments $BR$ and $CP$ meet at $F$. Calculate $$\frac{\operatorname{Area}(ABC)}{\operatorname{Area}(DEF)}.$$

cl.2015.0.1.reviewed_statement: Determine the number of pairs of functions $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, $$f(g(n))=n+2015,\qquad g(f(n))=n^2+2015.$$
cl.2015.0.1.rationale: Integer-valued functions are constrained by composition equations.

cl.2015.0.2.reviewed_statement: In the country of Muilejistan, a network of roads connects all its cities. Between any two cities there is exactly one route without backtracking, that is, one route in which a traveller never returns along the road just travelled. The longest possible route between two cities has length $600$ kilometres. For example, the route from Mlar to Nlar is $600$ kilometres long, and the route from Klar to Glar is also $600$ kilometres long. (a) Jalim leaves Mlar for Nlar at noon, and Kalim leaves Klar for Glar at noon. If they travel at the same speed, prove that they meet somewhere along their routes. (b) If the distance in kilometres between each pair of cities is an integer, prove that the distance in kilometres from Glar to Mlar is even.

cl.2015.0.3.reviewed_statement: Prove that the orthocentre, incentre and circumcentre of an acute scalene triangle are not collinear.

cl.2015.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $x,y>0$ be real numbers. Prove that $$\left(1+\frac1x\right)\left(1+\frac1y\right)\ge\left(1+\frac2{x+y}\right)^2.$$

cl.2016.0.1.reviewed_statement: An equilateral triangle of side length $20$ is subdivided by lines parallel to its sides into $20^2=400$ equilateral triangles of side length $1$. Some unit segments that are sides of these small triangles are to be coloured red, so that no small triangle has all three sides red. Determine the largest possible number of unit segments that can be coloured red.
cl.2016.0.1.rationale: An extremal edge colouring is imposed on a triangular geometric subdivision.

cl.2016.0.2.reviewed_statement: There are $2016$ points near a line such that the distance from each point to the line is less than $1$ centimetre, and the distance between any two points is greater than $2$ centimetres. Prove that two of the points are at distance at least $17$ metres.
cl.2016.0.2.rationale: A finite point configuration in a narrow strip forces a geometric distance bound.

cl.2016.0.3.reviewed_statement: A set $A$ of integers is called admissible if, whenever $x,y\in A$, we have $$x^2+kxy+y^2\in A$$ for every integer $k$. Determine all pairs of nonzero integers $m,n$ for which the only admissible set containing both $m$ and $n$ is the set of all integers.

cl.2016.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $f,g$ be nonzero polynomials with integer coefficients and $\deg f>\deg g$. Suppose that the polynomial $pf+g$ has a rational root for infinitely many primes $p$. Prove that $f$ has a rational root. A rational root of a polynomial $f$ is a number $q\in\mathbb Q$ such that $f(q)=0$.
cl.2016.0.4.rationale: Rational roots of integer polynomials are constrained for infinitely many prime parameters.

cl.2022.0.1.reviewed_statement: The sets of rational numbers $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_5\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_5\}$ both contain $0$ and satisfy $$\{a_i+b_j:1\le i,j\le5\}=\{0,1,2,\ldots,24\}.$$ Determine these sets. The set on the left consists of all possible sums of an element of $A$ and an element of $B$.
cl.2022.0.1.rationale: Additive representations by two rational sets exhaust a finite integer interval.

cl.2022.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB\ne AC$. Let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$, and $E$ the intersection of the bisector of $\angle BAC$ with $BC$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the second intersections of the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$ with $AC$ and $AB$, respectively. Prove that lines $AD,BP,CQ$ are concurrent.

cl.2022.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a natural number with more than $2021$ decimal digits, none of which is $8$ or $9$. Suppose that $n$ is relatively prime to $2021$. Prove that one digit of $n$ can be increased by at most $2$ so that the resulting number is divisible by $2021$.
cl.2022.0.3.rationale: Decimal digit changes and a divisibility condition combine a finite choice with modular arithmetic.

cl.2023.2.7.reviewed_statement: A function $f$ on the nonnegative integers satisfies: (i) $f(n)$ is an integer for every $n$; (ii) $f(0)=1$; (iii) $$f(n+1)>f(n)+f(n-1)+\cdots+f(0)$$ for every $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. Determine the smallest possible value of $f(2023)$.

cl.2023.2.8.reviewed_statement: Determine the smallest positive integer $n$ with the following property: for every triple of positive integers $x,y,z$ such that $x\mid y^3$, $y\mid z^3$ and $z\mid x^3$, we also have $$xyz\mid(x+y+z)^n.$$

cl.2023.2.9.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB<AC$, and let $\omega$ be its circumcircle. cl.2024.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c>0$ satisfy $a+b+c\le\frac32$. Find the minimum of $$a+b+c+\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c.$$

cl.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $m\ge2$ and $k\ge1$ be integers. Prove that $$(m-1)^2\mid m^k-1\quad\text{if and only if}\quad m-1\mid k.$$

cl.2024.1.3.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$. Let $P$ lie on segment $CD$. Let $Q$ be the intersection of lines $AP$ and $CB$, and $R$ the intersection of lines $BP$ and $CA$. Prove that $\angle RDC=\angle QDC$.

cl.2024.1.4.reviewed_statement: Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. Prove that if none of $f(-1),f(0),f(1)$ is divisible by $3$, then $f(m)\ne0$ for every integer $m$.

cl.2026.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_{2026})$ be a sequence of positive integers, not necessarily distinct. Let $m$ be the number of triples $(i,j,k)$ with $1\le i<j<k\le2026$ such that $$a_i+1=a_j=a_k-1.$$ Find the largest possible value of $m$ over all such sequences $A$.

th.2006.1.17.reviewed_statement: Six people of distinct weights form a triangular arrangement with three people in the bottom row, two in the middle row, and one at the top. Each person in the top two rows must weigh less than each of the two people supporting them. How many distinct arrangements are there?

th.2006.1.18.reviewed_statement: The traffic police select $10$ days in May for patrols, with no two selected days consecutive. In how many ways can they select the days?

th.2006.2.19.reviewed_statement: Prove that the product of three consecutive positive integers is never a perfect square.

th.2006.2.20.reviewed_statement: From a point $P$ outside a circle, tangents are drawn touching it at $A,C$. A point $B$ lies on segment $AC$, and segment $PB$ meets the circle at $Q$. The bisector of $\angle AQC$ meets $AC$ at $R$. Prove that $\frac{AB}{BC}=\left(\frac{AR}{RC}\right)^2$.

th.2006.2.21.reviewed_statement: Let $P(x),Q(x),R(x)$ be polynomials satisfying $$2xP(x^3)+Q(-x-x^3)=(1+x+x^2)R(x).$$ Prove that $x-1$ divides $P(x)-Q(x)$.

th.2006.2.22.reviewed_statement: A class of $28$ students is divided into four groups of seven. In each group the students are labelled $1,2,\ldots,7$ in some order. Prove that, regardless of the labels, four students of the same gender come from two groups and share the same two labels. For this problem assume that there are two genders.

th.2006.2.23.reviewed_statement: Prove that there are coprime positive integers $m,n$ for which $$2549\mid(25\cdot49)^m+25^n-2\cdot49^n.$$

th.2006.2.24.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers. Prove that $$1+\frac3{ab+bc+ca}\ge\frac6{a+b+c}.$$

th.2007.1.1.reviewed_statement: In a circle with centre $O$, radii $OA,OB$ are perpendicular. Chord $AC$ meets $OB$ at $E$, and arc $AC$ has length one third of the circumference. A point $D\in OB$ satisfies $CD\perp AB$. If $AC$ is $2$ units longer than $OD$, find $AC$.

th.2007.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with equal arcs $AB,BC$. Given $AD=6$, $BD=4$, $CD=1$, compute $AB$.

th.2007.1.3.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ has $\angle B=90^\circ$. A circle is tangent to $AB$ at $B$ and to $AC$. Another circle is tangent to the first circle and to both sides $AB,AC$. If $AB=\sqrt3$ and $BC=3$, find the radius of the second circle.

th.2007.1.4.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ has $AC=16$, $BC=12$. Points $E\in AC,F\in BC$ satisfy $CE=3CF$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$, and let lines $EF,CM$ meet at $G$. Find $EG:GF$.

th.2007.1.5.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ has $\angle A=90^\circ$. A point $D$ lies on $AC$, and $F$ is the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$. If $BD=DC=CF=2$, find $AC$.

th.2007.1.6.reviewed_statement: Let $M$ be the midpoint of a given segment $BC$. A point $A$ is chosen to maximise $\angle ABC$, subject to $\angle MAC=20^\circ$. Find $BC/BA$.

th.2007.1.7.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be complex numbers with $a+b+c=1$, $a^2+b^2+c^2=2$, $a^3+b^3+c^3=3$. Find $a^4+b^4+c^4$.

th.2007.1.8.reviewed_statement: Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{84}$ be the roots of $x^{84}+7x-6=0$. Compute $\sum_{k=1}^{84}\frac{x_k}{x_k-1}$.

th.2007.1.9.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(x^2+x+3)+2f(x^2-3x+5)=6x^2-10x+17$ for all real numbers $x$. Find $f(85)$.

th.2007.1.10.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest positive integer $n$ for which $\sqrt3z^{n+1}-z^n-1=0$ has a root on the unit circle.
th.2007.1.10.rationale: The statement combines algebra and geometry conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2007.1.11.reviewed_statement: Find the number of functions $f:\{1,2,\ldots,2550\}\to\{61,80,84\}$ for which $\sum_{k=1}^{2550}f(k)$ is divisible by $3$.
th.2007.1.11.rationale: The statement combines combinatorics and number theory conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2007.1.12.reviewed_statement: An alien with four feet puts on four identical socks and four identical shoes, with the sock on each foot put on before the shoe. In how many orders can the alien put them on?

th.2007.1.13.reviewed_statement: Let $S=\{1,2,\ldots,8\}$. In how many ways can two disjoint subsets of $S$ be selected?

th.2007.1.14.reviewed_statement: The sum $\sum_{k=84}^{8000}\binom{k}{84}\binom{8084-k}{84}$ can be written as a binomial coefficient $\binom ab$, where $a,b$ are integers. Find one possible pair $(a,b)$.

th.2007.1.16.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest positive integer having $24$ positive divisors.

th.2007.1.17.reviewed_statement: Compute the product of all positive integers $n$ for which $n^2+59n+881$ is a perfect square.

th.2007.1.18.reviewed_statement: Let $p_k$ be the $k$th prime. Find the remainder when $\sum_{k=2}^{2550}p_k^{p_k^4-1}$ is divided by $2550$.

th.2007.2.19.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $$\sum_{i=1}^{2549}f(x_i+x_{i+1})+f\left(\sum_{i=1}^{2550}x_i\right)\le\sum_{i=1}^{2550}f(2x_i)$$ for all real numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{2550}$.

th.2007.2.20.reviewed_statement: At a dance party there are $n$ girls and $n$ boys, and $m$ songs are played. Each song is danced to by at least one boy–girl pair, and each member of every such pair receives one malai (garland). Prove that, for each positive integer $k\le n$, one can select $k$ boys and $n-k$ girls who received at least $m$ malai in total.

th.2007.2.21.reviewed_statement: Two circles meet at $X,Y$. The line through their centres meets the first at $A,C$ and the second at $B,D$, in the order $A,B,C,D$. Chord $XY$ meets $BC$ at $P$. Choose a point $O$ on segment $XP$. Lines $CO,BO$ meet the first and second circles again at $M,N$, respectively. If $AM,DN$ meet at $Z$, prove that $X,Y,Z$ are collinear.

th.2007.2.22.reviewed_statement: Find all primes $p$ for which $\frac{2^{p-1}-1}{p}$ is a perfect square.

th.2007.2.23.reviewed_statement: A school freshman class of $229$ boys and $271$ girls is divided into ten rooms of $50$ students, numbered $1$ to $50$ within each room. A relay team must contain either one boy and three girls, or one girl and three boys. It must consist of two pairs of equally numbered students from two rooms. Prove that the number of possible teams is odd.

th.2007.2.24.reviewed_statement: A triangle has perimeter $2s$, inradius $r$, and incentre $I$. Let $s_a,s_b,s_c$ be the distances from $I$ to its three vertices. Prove that $$\frac34+\frac r{s_a}+\frac r{s_b}+\frac r{s_c}\le\frac{s^2}{12r^2}.$$
th.2007.2.24.rationale: The statement combines geometry and algebra conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2008.1.1.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$ and $\angle ABC=60^\circ$. A point $E\in BC$ satisfies $BE:EC=3:2$. Compute $\cos\angle CAE$.

th.2008.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $AD$ be the common chord of two circles of equal radius. Points $B,C$ lie on the first and second circles, respectively, with $D\in BC$. Given $AB=15$, $AD=13$, $BC=18$, find the ratio of the inradii of triangles $ABD,ACD$.

th.2008.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find all positive real solutions of $$x+\left\lfloor\frac x3\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor\frac{2x}3\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{3x}5\right\rfloor.$$

th.2008.1.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that $$\sqrt{a^2+b^2-\sqrt2ab}+\sqrt{b^2+c^2-\sqrt2bc}\ge\sqrt{a^2+c^2}$$ for all positive real numbers $a,b,c$.

th.2008.1.5.reviewed_statement: Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree $2008$ whose roots are all real and such that, for every real number $\alpha$, $P(\alpha)=0$ implies $P(\alpha+1)=1$. Prove that $P$ has a repeated root.

th.2008.1.6.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y)|<1$ for all real numbers $x,y$. Prove that $\left|f\left(\frac x{2008}\right)-\frac{f(x)}{2008}\right|<1$ for every real number $x$.

th.2008.1.8.reviewed_statement: Prove that $2551\cdot543^n-2008\cdot7^n$ is never a perfect square for a positive integer $n$.

th.2008.1.9.reviewed_statement: Find the number of pairs of sets $(A,B)$ with $A\subseteq B\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots,10\}$.

th.2008.1.10.reviewed_statement: Seventeen points are added on the sides of triangle $ABC$, giving $20$ points in total including its vertices. Find the maximum number of nondegenerate triangles with vertices among these points.
th.2008.1.10.rationale: The statement combines combinatorics and geometry conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2008.2.11.reviewed_statement: A point $P$ lies outside a circle $\omega$, and its tangents touch the circle at $A,B$. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $AP,AB$, respectively. Line $MN$ meets $\omega$ at $C$, with $N$ between $M,C$. Line $PC$ meets $\omega$ again at $D$, and $ND$ meets $PB$ at $O$. Prove that $MNOP$ is a rhombus.

th.2008.2.12.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $N$ such that (i) $N$ has at least two distinct prime factors; and (ii) if $d_1<d_2<d_3<d_4$ are its four smallest divisors, then $N=d_1^2+d_2^2+d_3^2+d_4^2$.

th.2008.2.13.reviewed_statement: For each positive integer $n$, put $a_n=n(n+1)$. Prove that $$n^{1/a_1}+n^{1/a_3}+n^{1/a_5}+\cdots+n^{1/a_{2n-1}}\ge n^{a_{3n+2}/a_{3n+1}}.$$

th.2008.2.14.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that $$\binom{2n+1}{1}-\binom{2n+1}{3}2008+\binom{2n+1}{5}2008^2-\cdots+(-1)^n\binom{2n+1}{2n+1}2008^n$$ is not divisible by $19$.
th.2008.2.14.rationale: The statement combines number theory and combinatorics conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2008.2.15.reviewed_statement: A class of $m$ boys and $n$ girls lines up. Over all possible orders, find the average number of adjacent pairs consisting of two boys or two girls.

th.2008.2.16.reviewed_statement: Let $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfy $f(xy)^2=f(x^2)f(y^2)$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$ with $x^2y^3>2008$. Prove that the same identity holds for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

th.2009.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $S$ be a set of positive integers such that $a+b$ is a perfect square whenever $a,b\in S$ are distinct. Given $2009,2087\in S$, find the maximum possible size of $S$.

th.2009.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $k,n$ be positive integers with $k<n$. Find the number of subsets of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ whose largest and smallest elements differ by $k$.

th.2009.1.3.reviewed_statement: Teeradet is in a class of $19$ students. They form nonempty clubs, and a student may belong to several clubs. Any two clubs differ in at least one student, and every club containing Teeradet has an odd number of students. Find the maximum possible number of clubs.

th.2009.1.4.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Points $E,F\in AC$ satisfy $AF=FE=EC$. Segment $AD$ meets $BE,BF$ at $G,H$, respectively. Find the ratio of the areas of triangles $BGH,ABC$.

th.2009.1.5.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $$f(xy+2x+2y-1)=f(x)f(y)+f(y)+x-2$$ for all real numbers $x,y$.

th.2009.1.6.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB>AC$, and its incircle touches $BC$ at $D$. Let $DE$ be a diameter of the incircle, and let $F$ be the intersection of line $AE$ with side $BC$. Find the ratio of the areas of triangles $DEF,ABC$ in terms of the side lengths of $ABC$.

th.2009.1.7.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be real numbers and put $S_n=a^n+b^n+c^n$ for positive integers $n$. Suppose that $S_1,S_2,S_3$ are integers and $6\mid5S_1-3S_2-2S_3$. Prove that $S_n$ is an integer for every positive integer $n$.
th.2009.1.7.rationale: The statement combines algebra and number theory conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2009.1.8.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be the side lengths of a triangle and put $s=\frac{a+b+c}2$. Prove that $$\frac{2a(2a-s)}{b+c}+\frac{2b(2b-s)}{c+a}+\frac{2c(2c-s)}{a+b}\ge s.$$
th.2009.1.8.rationale: The statement combines algebra and geometry conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2009.1.9.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, $D,E$ are the midpoints of $BC,AC$, respectively, and $AD,BE$ meet at $P$. If $\angle CAD=15^\circ$ and $\angle APB=60^\circ$, find $\frac{AB}{BC}$.

th.2009.1.10.reviewed_statement: Let $p\ge5$ be prime, and write $$\frac1{2^2}+\frac1{4^2}+\frac1{6^2}+\cdots+\frac1{(p-1)^2}=\frac ab$$ in lowest terms. Prove that $p\mid a$.

th.2009.2.11.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b$ be integers and $p$ a prime. For each positive integer $k$, define $A_k=\{n\in\mathbb Z_{>0}:p^k\mid a^n-b^n\}$. Prove that if $A_1$ is nonempty, then $A_k$ is nonempty for every positive integer $k$.

th.2009.2.12.reviewed_statement: Does there exist an injective function $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Q$ satisfying $f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all positive integers $x,y$?
th.2009.2.12.rationale: The statement combines algebra and number theory conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2009.2.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral whose diagonals meet at $M$ and for which $MA\cdot MC+MA\cdot CD=MB\cdot MD$. The bisector of $\angle ACD$ meets ray $BA$ at $K$. Prove that $BC=DK$ if and only if $AB\parallel CD$.

th.2009.2.14.reviewed_statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer. Prove that $$(m-n)^2=kmn+m+n$$ has infinitely many positive integer solutions $(m,n)$.

th.2009.2.15.reviewed_statement: A class contains $80$ boys and $80$ girls. On each weekday from Monday to Friday before final exams, the teacher makes $16$ books available to borrow. Each book can be borrowed for only one day at a time, and each student can borrow only once during the week. Prove that there are two days and two books for which either (i) neither book was borrowed on either day; or (ii) both books were borrowed on both days, and the four borrowers were all boys or all girls.

th.2009.2.16.reviewed_statement: Find all polynomials $$P(x)=(-1)^nx^n+a_1x^{n-1}+a_2x^{n-2}+\cdots+a_{n-1}x+a_n$$ such that (i) $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\}=\{0,1\}$; and (ii) all roots of $P$ are distinct real numbers.

th.2010.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find the number of ways to distribute $11$ balls among five boxes of different sizes, with at least one ball in each, so that the largest and smallest boxes together contain more balls than the other three boxes together.

th.2010.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB=AC$. A circle through $B,C$ meets $AB,AC$ again at $D,E$, respectively. A point $F$ on the circle satisfies $EF\perp BC$. If $BC=x$, $CF=y$, $BF=z$, express $DF$ in terms of $x,y,z$.

th.2010.1.3.reviewed_statement: Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which the integer $2\underbrace{55\cdots5}_{n\text{ digits}}3$ is divisible by $2553$.

th.2010.1.4.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be equilateral. Points $M\in AB,N\in AC$ satisfy $AN=BM$ and $3MB=AB$. Lines $CM,BN$ meet at $O$. Find $\angle AOB$.

th.2010.1.5.reviewed_statement: In a round-robin table-tennis tournament with $2010$ athletes, each match has a winner and a loser. Let $a_i,b_i$ be the numbers of wins and losses of athlete $i$. Prove that $\sum_{i=1}^{2010}a_i^2=\sum_{i=1}^{2010}b_i^2$.

th.2010.1.6.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $$f(3x+y)+f(3x-y)=f(x+y)+f(x-y)+16f(x)$$ for all real numbers $x,y$. Prove that $f(-x)=f(x)$ for every real number $x$.

th.2010.1.7.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers. Prove that $$\frac{a^5}{bc^2}+\frac{b^5}{ca^2}+\frac{c^5}{ab^2}\ge a^2+b^2+c^2.$$

th.2010.1.8.reviewed_statement: For integers $x,y$, define their distance modulo $2553$, denoted $d(x,y)$, as the smallest nonnegative integer congruent to either $x-y$ or $y-x$ modulo $2553$. Prove that every set $S$ of integers with $|S|\ge70$ contains $m,n$ with $d(m,n)\le36$.
th.2010.1.8.rationale: The statement combines number theory and combinatorics conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2010.1.9.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be real numbers such that all roots of $2x^5+5x^4+5x^3+ax^2+bx+c=0$ are real. Find the smallest real root.

th.2010.1.10.reviewed_statement: Find all primes $p$ for which $\binom{100}{p}+7$ is divisible by $p$.
th.2010.1.10.rationale: The statement combines number theory and combinatorics conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2010.2.11.reviewed_statement: Prove that for every positive integer $x$, there is a $y\in\{2,5,13\}$ such that $xy-1$ is not a perfect square.

th.2010.2.12.reviewed_statement: The Ministry of Education selects $2010$ students from five regions of Thailand for a debate tournament. Every pair debates one of three topics: politics, economics, or societal problems. Prove that three students were born in the same month, come from the same region, have the same gender, and debate the same topic in each pair. For this problem assume that there are two genders.

th.2010.2.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be scalene with $AB<BC<CA$. Let $D,E$ be the projections of $A$ onto the internal bisectors of $\angle ABC,\angle ACB$, respectively. Line $DE$ meets sides $AB,AC$ at $M,N$, respectively. Prove that $\frac{AB+AC}{BC}=\frac{DE}{MN}+1$.

th.2010.2.14.reviewed_statement: For $i=1,2$, let a triangle have side lengths $a_i,b_i,c_i$ and corresponding altitude lengths $p_i,q_i,r_i$. Define $$a_3=\sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2},\qquad b_3=\sqrt{b_1^2+b_2^2},\qquad c_3=\sqrt{c_1^2+c_2^2}.$$ Prove that $a_3,b_3,c_3$ are the side lengths of a triangle, and that its corresponding altitudes satisfy $p_3^2\ge p_1^2+p_2^2$, $q_3^2\ge q_1^2+q_2^2$, $r_3^2\ge r_1^2+r_2^2$.
th.2010.2.14.rationale: The statement combines geometry and algebra conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2010.2.15.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $$f(x-t,y)+f(x+t,y)+f(x,y-t)+f(x,y+t)=2010$$ for all real numbers $x,y$ and all nonzero real numbers $t$.

th.2010.2.16.reviewed_statement: Prove that no primes $p,q,r$ satisfy $p>r$, $q>r$, and $pq\mid r^p+r^q$.

th.2011.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge3$ be an integer, and let $p,q$ be primes satisfying $p\mid n!$ and $q\mid(n-1)!-1$. Prove that $p<q$.

th.2011.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f$ on the positive integers satisfying $f(2m+2n)=f(m)f(n)$ for all positive integers $m,n$.

th.2011.1.3.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$. A point $D$ lies strictly inside it, and lines $AD,BD,CD$ meet $BC,CA,AB$ at $P,Q,R$, respectively. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $PQ$. Prove that if $\angle BRP=\angle PRC$, then $MR=MC$.

th.2011.1.4.reviewed_statement: An international school has $900$ students, including $59$ international boys and $59$ international girls. They are divided into $30$ classrooms of $30$ students, numbered $1$ to $30$ in each classroom, such that either (i) no two international students in the same classroom have consecutive numbers; or (ii) in all classrooms the student numbered $1$ is a boy. Prove that there are four international students $A,B,C,D$ of the same gender such that $A,B$ are in one classroom, $C,D$ are in a different classroom, and the difference between the numbers of $A,B$ equals the difference between the numbers of $C,D$.

th.2011.1.5.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ such that $n=d(n)^4$, where $d(n)$ is the number of positive divisors of $n$.

th.2011.1.6.reviewed_statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_{2011}\in[0,1]$, and let $m=\frac1{2011}(x_1+\cdots+x_{2011})$. Find the maximum of $\sum_{i=1}^{2011}(x_i-m)^2$.

th.2011.2.7.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive real numbers such that all roots of $x^5-ax^4+bx^3-cx^2+dx=1$ are real. Prove that $\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c+\frac1d\le\frac35$.

th.2011.2.8.reviewed_statement: Let $G$ be the centroid of triangle $ABC$. If line $AC$ is tangent to the circumcircle of $ABG$, prove that $AB+BC\le2AC$.

th.2011.2.9.reviewed_statement: Prove that $1+\frac13+\frac15+\cdots+\frac1{2n-1}$ is not an integer for any integer $n>1$.

th.2011.2.10.reviewed_statement: Does there exist a function $f$ on the positive integers satisfying $f(m+f(n))=f(m)+f(n)+f(n+1)$ for all positive integers $m,n$?

th.2011.2.11.reviewed_statement: The incircle of triangle $ABC$ touches $BC,CA,AB$ at $X,Y,Z$, respectively. Let $I_a,I_b,I_c$ be the excentres opposite $A,B,C$. Prove that the incentre of $ABC$, the centroid of $I_aI_bI_c$, and the orthocentre of $XYZ$ are collinear.

th.2011.2.12.reviewed_statement: There are $7662$ chairs in a circle around Chiang Mai, each labelled for first-, second-, or third-grade students, with $2554$ chairs of each label. First-, second-, and third-grade students, $2554$ of each grade, receive footballs, basketballs, and volleyballs, respectively. They sit on chairs labelled for their grade. Then all students simultaneously pass their balls to the student on their left, repeated a positive number of times. A chair labelling is called lin-ping if it is possible for all first-, second-, and third-grade students to hold volleyballs, footballs, and basketballs, respectively. Find the number of lin-ping labellings.

th.2012.1.1.reviewed_statement: In right triangle $ABC$, $\angle B=90^\circ$. A point $P$ lies on $BC$, and the circle with diameter $CP$ meets $AC,AP$ again at $Q,R$, respectively. Prove that $CP^2=AC\cdot CQ-AP\cdot PR$.

th.2012.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2012}$ be pairwise distinct integers. Prove that $(x-a_1)\cdots(x-a_{2012})=(1006!)^2$ has at most one integer solution.

th.2012.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $m,n>1$ be coprime odd integers. Prove that $$\left\lfloor\frac{m^{\varphi(n)+1}+n^{\varphi(m)+1}}{mn}\right\rfloor$$ is even, where $\varphi$ is Euler’s totient function.

th.2012.1.4.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a unit square. Points $E,F,G,H$ lie outside it and satisfy $\angle AEB=\angle BFC=\angle CGD=\angle DHA=90^\circ$. Let $O_1,O_2,O_3,O_4$ be the incentres of triangles $ABE,BCF,CDG,DAH$, respectively. Prove that the area of quadrilateral $O_1O_2O_3O_4$ is at most $1$.

th.2012.1.5.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $f(f(x)+xf(y))=3f(x)+4xy$ for all real numbers $x,y$.

th.2012.1.6.reviewed_statement: At Hat Yai Witthayalai School, $n\ge100$ freshmen play a round-robin rock-paper-scissors tournament. A win earns $2$ points, a draw $1$, and a loss $0$. The Mathematics Department receives a computer exactly when every group of $100$ freshmen contains a student who beat all the other $99$ and another student who lost to all the other $99$. It receives a printer exactly when all total scores are pairwise distinct. Find the least possible $n$ for which receiving a computer always implies receiving a printer.

th.2012.2.7.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,m$ be integers with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $5\mid ma^2+b^2$. Prove that there is an integer $n$ such that $5\mid m-n^2$.

th.2012.2.8.reviewed_statement: A round-robin taekwondo tournament has $4n$ students, $2n$ boys and $2n$ girls. In a match between students of the same gender, a win, draw, and loss earn $3,1,0$ points. In a boy–girl match, a boy earns $2$ points for a win and $0$ otherwise; a girl earns $3,2,0$ points for a win, draw, and loss, respectively. Let $P$ be the number of drawn matches and $Q$ the total number of matches. If the maximum total score is $4n-1$, find $P/Q$.

th.2012.2.9.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and $P(x)=x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1x+1$ a polynomial with positive real coefficients and all roots real. Prove that $P(x)\ge(x+1)^n$ for every $x>0$.

Line $RP$ meets $BA,BC$ at $T,M$, respectively. Choose $N\in TB$ so that $NM$ bisects $\angle TMB$. Let $K=CN\cap TM$ and $H=BK\cap CD$. Prove that $\angle NMH=90^\circ$.

th.2022.2.10.reviewed_statement: For positive integers $u,n$, call $u$ a friend of $n$ if there is a positive multiple $N$ of $n$ whose decimal digit sum is $u$. Find all positive integers $n$ having only finitely many positive integers that are not friends of $n$.

th.2024.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral. Points $S\in AD,T\in AB$ satisfy $AS=AT$, and points $U\in BC,V\in CD$ satisfy $CU=CV$. Suppose $BT=BU$ and lines $ST,UV,BD$ are concurrent. Prove that $AB+CD=BC+AD$.

th.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs of positive integers $(m,n)$ for which both $\frac{m^5+n}{m^2+n^2}$ and $\frac{m+n^5}{m^2+n^2}$ are integers.

th.2024.1.3.reviewed_statement: Given a positive real number $c$, find all functions $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying $x^2f(xf(y))f(x)f(y)=c$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

th.2024.1.4.reviewed_statement: Each cell of an $88\times253$ table is purple or yellow. For each yellow cell $c$, let $x(c),y(c)$ be the numbers of purple cells in its row and column, respectively. Suppose $x(c)y(c)\ge184$ for every yellow cell. Find the minimum possible number of purple cells.

th.2024.1.5.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute scalene triangle, with altitude foot $D$ from $A$ to $BC$ and orthocentre $H$. Points $S,T$ lie on its circumcircle with $\angle BSH=\angle CTH=90^\circ$. If $AH=2HD$, prove that $D,S,T$ are collinear.

th.2024.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ for which the elements of $\{1,2,\ldots,2n+1\}\setminus\{n+1\}$ can be divided into two groups of equal size and equal sum.
th.2024.2.6.rationale: The statement combines number theory and combinatorics conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2024.2.7.reviewed_statement: Let $m,n$ be positive integers with $n\le m\le2n$. Find the number of complex tuples $(z_1,\ldots,z_m)$ satisfying $z_1^7+\cdots+z_m^7=n$ and $z_k^3-2z_k^2+2z_k-1=0$ for every $k=1,\ldots,m$.
th.2024.2.7.rationale: The statement combines algebra and combinatorics conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2024.2.8.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex hexagon and let $U,V,W,X,Y,Z$ be the midpoints of $AB,BC,CD,DE,EF,FA$, respectively. Prove that $UX,VY,WZ$ are the side lengths of a triangle. A convex polygon has all its interior angles less than $180^\circ$.

th.2024.2.9.reviewed_statement: Prove that for every positive integer $n$, there are positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n,d_1,\ldots,d_n$ such that (i) $d_i\mid\binom{2a_i}{a_i}$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$; (ii) $d_{i+1}=d_i+1$ for $i=1,\ldots,n-1$; and (iii) $d_i\ne m^k$ for every $i=1,\ldots,n$ and all positive integers $m,k$ with $k\ge2$.
th.2024.2.9.rationale: The statement combines number theory and combinatorics conditions; both are substantive to the requested assertion or count.

th.2024.2.10.reviewed_statement: Find the maximum of $abcd(a+b)(b+c)(c+d)(d+a)$ over positive real numbers $a,b,c,d$ satisfying $\sqrt[3]a+\sqrt[3]b+\sqrt[3]c+\sqrt[3]d=4$.

se.2025.0.1.reviewed_statement: In a convex pentagon $ABCDE$, $\angle EAB=\angle ABC=90^\circ$ and $BC=CD=DE=EA=1$ cm. Segments $AC,BD$ meet perpendicularly at $F$. Find the lengths of $AC,BD$.

se.2025.0.2.reviewed_statement: A genuine coin weighs $4$ grams and a counterfeit coin weighs $3$ grams. You have six coins and a scale that measures weight exactly, rather than a balance scale. Prove that five weighings always suffice to identify all counterfeit coins.

se.2025.0.3.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $$f(f(f(f(f(x+y)))))=f(f(x))+y+1$$ for all real numbers $x,y$.

se.2025.0.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that $a^6+b^6+c^6=d^6+e^6$ has no solution with all of $a,b,c,d,e$ prime.

se.2025.0.5.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle ACB=60^\circ$. The bisector of this angle meets $AB$ at $D$. Construct equilateral triangles $AED,BDF$, with $E,F$ on the opposite side of $AB$ from $C$. Let $O$ be the circumcentre of $ABC$. Lines $CO,AB$ meet at $G$, and lines $CD,EF$ meet at $H$. Prove that $DH=GH$.

se.2025.0.6.reviewed_statement: For which integers $n$ can a regular $n$-gon be cut into $2025$ regular polygons, not necessarily of the same shape, with no pieces left over?
se.2025.0.6.rationale: Regular polygon geometry constrains a combinatorial dissection into a specified number of pieces.

tht.2011.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integer pairs $(m,n)$ for which an $m\times n$ table can be coloured black and white so that, for every unit square $U$, the number of unit squares $V$ sharing a vertex with $U$ and having the same colour as $U$ is odd.

tht.2011.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(x+y)|=|f(x)+f(y)|$ for all real numbers $x,y$. Prove that $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all real numbers $x,y$.

tht.2011.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be acute with $AB>AC$ and altitude $AD$. The circle with diameter $BC$ meets $AC$ at $E$, and its tangents at $B,E$ meet at $X$. Lines $AX,BC$ meet at $Y$. Prove that $\frac1{DC}-\frac1{BD}=\frac2{DY}$.

tht.2011.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $f(x),g(x)$ be polynomials with rational coefficients whose product has integer coefficients. Prove that the product of any coefficient of $f$ and any coefficient of $g$ is an integer.
tht.2011.2.4.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive algebra and number theory conditions.

tht.2011.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $p,q$ be odd primes and $m$ a positive integer with $
u_q(p-1)=m$. Prove that, for every integer $n\ge0$, the order of $p$ modulo $q^{m+n}$ is $q^n$ and $
u_q(p^{q^n}-1)=m+n$. Here $
u_q(x)$ is the largest integer $k$ such that $q^k\mid x$.

tht.2011.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB\le AC$, and let an interior point $P$ lie on the bisector of $\angle BAC$. Choose $D\in PC,E\in PB$ with $\angle PBD=\angle PCE$. Lines $BD,AC$ meet at $X$, and lines $CE,AB$ meet at $Y$. Prove that $BX\le CY$.

tht.2011.3.8.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be acute with orthocentre $H$ and nine-point centre $N$. Points $Y\in CA,Z\in CB$ satisfy the directed-angle relations $\angle(AC,HY)=-\frac\pi3$ and $\angle(AB,HZ)=\frac\pi3$. Let $U$ be the circumcentre of $HYZ$. Prove that $A,N,U$ are collinear.

tht.2011.3.9.reviewed_statement: A graph has $2n$ vertices and $2n(n-1)$ edges, where $n>1$ is an integer. Prove that some vertices and edges can be coloured red so that both endpoints of every red edge are red and every red vertex belongs to exactly $n$ red edges.

tht.2011.4.10.reviewed_statement: A $16\times16$ matrix has entries $+1,-1$. For any two distinct columns, the sum of products of corresponding entries is nonpositive. Prove that there are at most $160$ entries equal to $+1$.
tht.2011.4.10.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive combinatorics and algebra conditions.

tht.2011.4.11.reviewed_statement: Find all primes $p$ for which integers $a,b$ exist with $p^2=a^2+b^2$ and $p\mid a^3+b^3-4$.

tht.2011.4.12.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ has circumcircle $\Gamma$ and inradius $1$. Let $\Gamma_A$ be the circle tangent to lines $AB,AC$ and internally tangent to $\Gamma$; define $\Gamma_B,\Gamma_C$ similarly. If their radii are $R_A,R_B,R_C$, prove that $R_A+R_B+R_C\ge4$.

tht.2011.5.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be acute, with altitude feet $D\in BC,E\in CA,F\in AB$. Let $P$ be either intersection of line $EF$ with the circumcircle. Lines $BP,DF$ meet at $Q$. Prove that $AP=AQ$.

tht.2011.5.14.reviewed_statement: Can all rational numbers be coloured with two colours so that distinct rational numbers $x,y$ have different colours whenever $xy=1$ or $x+y\in\{0,1\}$?
tht.2011.5.14.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive combinatorics and number theory conditions.

tht.2011.5.15.reviewed_statement: Define $x_1=1$, $x_{2k}=-x_k$, and $x_{2k-1}=(-1)^{k+1}x_k$ for $k\ge1$. Prove that $x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n\ge0$ for every $n\ge1$.
tht.2011.5.15.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive algebra and combinatorics conditions.

tht.2011.6.16.reviewed_statement: An $8\times8$ square is divided into $64$ unit squares. Diagonals are drawn in some cells so that no two share any point, including endpoints. Find the maximum possible number of drawn diagonals.
tht.2011.6.16.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive combinatorics and geometry conditions.

tht.2011.6.17.reviewed_statement: A circle $\Omega$ through vertex $A$ of triangle $ABC$ is tangent to segment $BC$ at $D$. Let $E$ be the projection of $D$ onto $AC$. Choose $F\in\Omega$ on the opposite side of line $EC$ from $D$, with $\angle EFC=2\angle ECD$. If $CF$ meets $\Omega$ again at $G$, prove that $AG\parallel BC$.

tht.2011.6.18.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest number $n$ for which polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ with rational coefficients satisfy $x^2+7=f_1(x)^2+\cdots+f_n(x)^2$.
tht.2011.6.18.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive algebra and number theory conditions.

tht.2011.7.19.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be real numbers with $ab+bc+ca=1$. Prove that $$\frac{(a+b)^2+1}{c^2+2}+\frac{(b+c)^2+1}{a^2+2}+\frac{(c+a)^2+1}{b^2+2}\ge3.$$

tht.2011.7.20.reviewed_statement: Find the least positive integer $n$ for which distinct positive integers $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ satisfy $$\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac1{s_i}\right)=\frac{51}{2010}.$$

tht.2011.7.21.reviewed_statement: The vertices $X,Y,Z$ of an equilateral triangle lie on sides $BC,CA,AB$, respectively, of an acute triangle $ABC$. Prove that the incentre of $ABC$ lies inside $XYZ$.

tht.2011.8.22.reviewed_statement: Points $D,E$ lie in the interiors of sides $AB,AC$ of triangle $ABC$, and line $DE$ meets the extension of $BC$ at $F$. Prove that $ADE$ is similar to the triangle whose vertices are the circumcentres of $ABC,DFB,EFC$.

tht.2011.8.23.reviewed_statement: Dreamland has $1024$ cities labelled $0,1,\ldots,1023$. Two cities are connected by one road exactly when their binary labels differ in one digit. Exactly eight roads are closed for repairs. Prove that a tourist can choose a closed route visiting every city exactly once using only open roads.

tht.2011.8.24.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb Q_{>0}$ satisfying $f(f(x)^2y)=x^3f(xy)$ for all positive rational numbers $x,y$.

tht.2011.9.26.reviewed_statement: For every integer $n\ge2$, let $A_n$ be the set of solutions of $x=\left\lfloor\frac x2\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac x3\right\rfloor+\cdots+\left\lfloor\frac xn\right\rfloor$. Prove that $A=\bigcup_{n\ge2}A_n$ is finite, and find $\max A$.

tht.2011.9.27.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCDE$ be a convex pentagon with $BC\parallel AE$, $AB=BC+AE$, and $\angle ABC=\angle CDE$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $CE$ and $O$ the circumcentre of $BCD$. If $\angle DMO=90^\circ$, prove that $2\angle BDA=\angle CDE$.

tht.2011.10.28.reviewed_statement: Define $K_0=1$ and $K_n=1+\min\{2K_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor},3K_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}\}$ for integers $n\ge1$. Prove or disprove that $K_n\ge n$ for every integer $n\ge0$.
tht.2011.10.28.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive algebra and combinatorics conditions.

tht.2011.10.29.reviewed_statement: A set of $n\ge4$ points has integer distance between every pair. Prove that at least one sixth of these distances are divisible by $3$.
tht.2011.10.29.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive geometry and number theory conditions.

tht.2011.10.30.reviewed_statement: In a round-robin tennis tournament with $n\ge4$ players, no game is drawn. Four players form a bad company if one lost to the other three, and each of those three won one and lost one game among themselves. Suppose no bad company exists. If player $i$ has $w_i$ wins and $l_i$ losses, prove that $\sum_{i=1}^n(w_i-l_i)^3\ge0$.
tht.2011.10.30.rationale: The requested assertion combines substantive combinatorics and algebra conditions.

tht.2011.11.31.reviewed_statement: Let real numbers $a,b,c,d$ satisfy $a+b+c+d=6$ and $a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=12$. Prove that $36\le4(a^3+b^3+c^3+d^3)-(a^4+b^4+c^4+d^4)\le48$.

tht.2011.11.32.reviewed_statement: Let $A_1\cdots A_n$ be a convex polygon. An interior point $P$ has projections $P_i$ onto lines $A_iA_{i+1}$ lying on their corresponding sides, with indices modulo $n$. Prove that for any $X_i\in A_iA_{i+1}$, $$\max\left\{\frac{X_1X_2}{P_1P_2},\ldots,\frac{X_nX_1}{P_nP_1}\right\}\ge1.$$

tht.2011.11.33.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b$ be integers and put $P(x)=ax^3+bx$. For a positive integer $n$, call $(a,b)$ n-good if $n\mid P(m)-P(k)$ implies $n\mid m-k$ for all integers $m,k$.
